content.content:
1	# Technical Assessment - Rent Collection
2	
3	Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router) - TypeScript - Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Storage) - Prisma - shadcn/ui - Tailwind CSS
4	Time: the timer above is what counts, normally 4 hours (about 30 min reading - 3 h building - 30 min write-ups and submission)
5	
6	## Read This First
7	
8	AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot...) are allowed and expected. We assess whether you understand and control what gets built. Code you cannot explain counts as not done.
9	
10	- Hidden tests. We run automated tests against every rule in this brief, including edge cases that are not in the examples:- your billing functions, about 50 hidden cases, run under TZ=UTC, TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur and TZ=America/New_York
11	- your HTTP API, called as each seeded account, including requests about other organizations' records and concurrent requests
12	- your Supabase Data API and Storage bucket, called directly with your publishable key and each user's token
13	- your payment webhook, with valid, forged, duplicated, concurrent and out-of-order callbacks
14	
15	- AI logs. Export the transcript of every AI session you use (in Claude Code: /export) into an ai-logs/ folder in your repo. We do not count how much you used AI. We look at how you directed it, what you checked and what you corrected.
16	- Walkthrough. If your submission passes, the interview starts with a 30-minute walkthrough of your code: we pick parts of it, ask "what happens if...", and ask you to make a small change live.
17	- Priorities. A correct and secure subset beats a complete but sloppy app. If time runs short, work in this order: billing functions (section 3), access control (6), payments (4), webhook (5), UI (9). Say in your README what you skipped.
18	- Names are a contract. Table names, column names, endpoint paths, file paths and response shapes in this brief are what our tests use. You may add more of your own.
19	
20	## 1. The Business
21	
22	You are building part of the rent collection module of a property management platform used by Malaysian property management companies.
23	
24	- Each organization (a property management company) rents units to tenants under leases.
25	- A lease produces invoices: an optional deposit, plus one rent invoice per monthly period.
26	- Tenants pay by cash, by bank transfer (with an uploaded slip), or online through a payment gateway. Payments are allocated to invoices.
27	- Business timezone: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no daylight saving). Currency: MYR (RM). 1 ringgit = 100 sen.
28	- Your server runs in UTC and our assessors work from several timezones. Every date and time the app shows or accepts is Malaysia time, whatever the timezone of the server or of the viewer's device.
29	
30	### Roles
31	
32	Role | Who | Can |
33	manager | Organization admin | Everything in their organization: create leases, record payments (approved immediately), approve, reject and void payments, read the audit log |
34	staff | Front desk | Read their organization's leases, invoices and payments; record payments (these wait for a manager's approval) |
35	tenant | Renter | Read their own profile, leases, invoices and payments; update their own phone number; pay online |
36	
37	A staff member or manager belongs to exactly one organization. Nobody ever sees another organization's data.
38	
39	## 2. Local Setup and Seed Data
40	
41	Develop against a local Supabase stack (Docker and the Supabase CLI), not a cloud project. See Supabase local development. We grade by running your project on our machine from a fresh clone, with exactly these commands:
42	npx supabase start # starts the stack from your supabase/config.toml
43	npx supabase db reset # rebuilds the database from supabase/migrations/
44	npm install
45	cp .env.example .env.local # we replace keys with the values from `npx supabase status` if they differ
46	npm run seed
47	npm run build && npm start
48	
49	- Commit supabase/config.toml, supabase/migrations/, and an .env.example that lists every variable your app needs, with local values and a comment saying where each one comes from.
50	- npm run seed creates exactly the data below on a freshly reset database, through your normal code paths (your lease creation and payment logic), so the invoices and allocations it produces are the ones your app would produce.
51	- All seeded accounts share one password of your choice, which you submit with your work.
52	
53	### Organizations and accounts
54	
55	Organization | Account | Role | Notes |
56	Northwind Properties | manager@northwind.test | manager | |
57	Northwind Properties | staff@northwind.test | staff | |
58	Northwind Properties | aisyah@northwind.test | tenant | Tenant "Aisyah Rahman" |
59	Northwind Properties | ben@northwind.test | tenant | Tenant "Ben Lim" |
60	Northwind Properties | probe@northwind.test | tenant | Tenant "Probe Tenant" (our tests create payments and leases for this tenant) |
61	Beta Realty | manager@beta.test | manager | |
62	Beta Realty | chen@beta.test | tenant | Tenant "Chen Wei" |
63	
64	### Units and leases
65	
66	Organization | Unit | Tenant | Start | End | Monthly rent | Deposit |
67	Northwind | A-12-3 | Aisyah Rahman | 2026-01-31 | 2026-07-15 | RM 1,500.00 | RM 3,000.00 |
68	Northwind | B-05-1 | Ben Lim | 2026-01-01 | 2026-04-15 | RM 1,000.29 | none |
69	Northwind | C-01-7 | Probe Tenant | 2026-02-28 | 2027-02-27 | RM 2,000.00 | RM 4,000.00 |
70	Northwind | D-03-2 | (no lease) | | | | |
71	Beta | KL-1 | Chen Wei | 2026-03-15 | 2027-03-14 | RM 2,200.00 | RM 4,400.00 |
72	
73	### Payments on Aisyah's lease
74	
75	- Cash, RM 3,000.00, received 2026-01-31 10:00 Malaysia time, recorded by the manager.
76	- Bank transfer, RM 2,000.00, received 2026-03-01 00:30 Malaysia time, recorded by staff with a slip file, then approved by the manager.
77	
78	## 3. Billing Rules - lib/billing.ts
79	
80	Create lib/billing.ts (or src/lib/billing.ts). It must be pure: no I/O, no imports from Next.js, React, Supabase or Prisma, and no dependence on the timezone of the machine it runs on. Your app must use it, and we test it directly.
81	export type InvoiceKind = 'deposit' | 'rent'
82	
83	export interface ScheduledInvoice {
84	kind: InvoiceKind
85	periodIndex: number | null // 0, 1, 2... for rent; null for the deposit
86	periodStart: string | null // 'YYYY-MM-DD'; null for the deposit
87	periodEnd: string | null // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive; null for the deposit
88	dueDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
89	amountSen: number // integer
90	}
91	
92	export function generateSchedule(lease: {
93	startDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
94	endDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive (the tenant's last day)
95	monthlyRentSen: number
96	depositSen: number
97	}): ScheduledInvoice[]
98	
99	export type InvoiceStatus = 'paid' | 'partially_paid' | 'unpaid' | 'overdue'
100	
101	export function invoiceStatus(
102	invoice: { dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number },
103	now: Date,
104	): InvoiceStatus
105	
106	export function parseRinggitToSen(input: string): number
107	
108	### generateSchedule
109	
110	- Validation. Throw an Error if a date is not a real calendar date written as YYYY-MM-DD, if endDate is before startDate, if monthlyRentSen is not a positive integer, or if depositSen is not a non-negative integer.
111	- Deposit. If depositSen > 0, the first invoice is the deposit: kind: 'deposit', due on startDate, period fields null.
112	- Anchors. Rent periods are anchored on the start date. The anchor of period k is the start date plus k calendar months, always counted from the start date (never from the previous anchor). If that month has fewer days than the start day, use the month's last day. A lease starting on Jan 31 has anchors Jan 31, Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31, Apr 30, and so on.
113	- Periods. Period k runs from anchor k to the day before anchor k+1, and is due on anchor k. There is a period for every anchor on or before endDate.
114	- Last period. It is cut at endDate. If it is shorter than its full length, it costs monthlyRentSen x days used / days in the full period, rounded half up to the nearest sen. Every other period costs monthlyRentSen.
115	- Order. The deposit first, then rent by period index.
116	  Worked example (Aisyah's lease):
117	  Period | Kind | Dates | Due | Amount |
118	  | deposit | | 2026-01-31 | RM 3,000.00 |
119	  0 | rent | 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-27 | 2026-01-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
120	  1 | rent | 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-30 | 2026-02-28 | RM 1,500.00 |
121	  2 | rent | 2026-03-31 to 2026-04-29 | 2026-03-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
122	  3 | rent | 2026-04-30 to 2026-05-30 | 2026-04-30 | RM 1,500.00 |
123	  4 | rent | 2026-05-31 to 2026-06-29 | 2026-05-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
124	  5 | rent | 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-15 | 2026-06-30 | RM 774.19 |
125	
126	Period 5 uses 16 of the 31 days from 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-30: 150000 x 16 / 31 = 77419.35, so 77419 sen.
127	
128	### invoiceStatus
129	
130	Apply these rules in order:
131	
132	- paid if paidSen >= amountSen.
133	- overdue if today's Malaysia date is after dueDate. An invoice due 2026-03-01 becomes overdue at 2026-03-02 00:00 Malaysia time (2026-03-01T16:00:00Z), not a moment earlier.
134	- partially_paid if paidSen > 0.
135	- Otherwise unpaid.
136	
137	### parseRinggitToSen
138	
139	Turns what a user types into sen. It accepts digits with optional comma thousands separators (groups of exactly three digits) and an optional decimal part of one or two digits, ignoring whitespace around the value: "1,500.50" gives 150050, "1.15" gives 115, "7" gives 700. Anything else throws an Error, for example "", "-5", "1.234", "1e3", "RM 10", "1,23".
140	
141	## 4. Payments
142	
143	### Recording a payment
144	
145	- Staff and managers record cash or bank transfer payments on a lease: the amount, the method, and the date and time the money was received (entered and shown in Malaysia time).
146	- A bank transfer needs a slip: a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB, stored in Supabase Storage (section 6). If recording fails after the upload, the file must not be left behind.
147	- A payment recorded by a manager is approved immediately. A payment recorded by staff is pending_verification until a manager approves or rejects it.
148	- Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.
149	
150	### Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)
151	
152	- Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
153	- Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
154	- Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.
155	- Payments are never deleted. Every approval, rejection, void and lease creation writes a row to audit_log (who, what, when, details).
156	
157	### Allocation
158	
159	When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.
160	The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.
161	All of this must stay correct when requests arrive at the same time. For example, two staff members recording payments on the same lease at once must not exceed the cap together, and a payment approved twice at once is allocated once.
162	
163	### Collections report
164	
165	The total of approved payments for each calendar month of received_at in Malaysia time, over a range of months, including months with nothing collected. With the seed data, Northwind's report for 2026-01 to 2026-03 is [{ month: '2026-01', collectedSen: 300000 }, { month: '2026-02', collectedSen: 0 }, { month: '2026-03', collectedSen: 200000 }].
166	
167	## 5. Online Payments
168	
169	A tenant pays online like this:
170	
171	- The tenant clicks Pay now on their lease. Your API creates a gateway bill for the amount due now: the unpaid amounts of the lease's invoices due on or before today's Malaysia date. If nothing is due, refuse. Bill ids must be impossible to guess.
172	- In production the tenant would now be redirected to the gateway. In this test, show the bill id and amount: we play the gateway using the simulator below.
173	- The gateway calls your webhook, POST /api/webhooks/gateway. Only the webhook can settle a bill. The gateway also sends the tenant back to /payments/return?bill_id=...&paid=true. That page only shows the bill's real status from your database and changes nothing.
174	
175	### Webhook
176	
177	The request body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with these fields. The gateway may add more fields in future.
178	Field | Example | Notes |
179	id | bill_8f3a2c | Your bill id (this short example is guessable; yours must not be) |
180	paid | true | true or false |
181	paid_amount | 210050 | Amount in sen; 0 when not paid |
182	paid_at | 2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800 | When it was paid |
183	transaction_id | TX-000123 | Gateway transaction id |
184	transaction_status | completed | completed, failed or pending |
185	x_signature | 06994f... | See below |
186	
187	Signature. Take every field in the request except x_signature, sort them by key (ascending by character code), write each one as the key immediately followed by the value, join them with |, and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the resulting string with your secret key GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY, as lowercase hex. Test vector, with the key test_x_signature_key and the six example values above:
188	source: idbill_8f3a2c|paidtrue|paid_amount210050|paid_at2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800|transaction_idTX-000123|transaction_statuscompleted
189	signature: 06994fab2d674e7829144eaa2204631716d3c099b503d38945e92b6296531641
190	Required behavior:
191	Situation | Response | Effect |
192	Signature missing or wrong | 401 | None |
193	Unknown bill id | 404 | None |
194	paid=true and paid_amount is not the bill's amount | 422 | None |
195	paid=true, bill pending or failed | 200 | Bill becomes paid, and one approved online payment is created with received_at = paid_at, then allocated |
196	paid=true, bill already paid (a repeat delivery) | 200 | None |
197	paid=false, bill pending | 200 | Bill becomes failed |
198	paid=false, bill already failed (a repeat delivery) | 200 | None |
199	paid=false, bill already paid (late or out of order) | 200 | None: a paid bill never goes back |
200	
201	The gateway retries, so it may deliver the same callback several times, including at the same moment. A bill creates at most one payment, ever. Never log the secret key or whole callback payloads.
202	
203	### Simulator
204	
205	Save this as gateway-sim.mjs and run node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false] with GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY set.
206	import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'
207	
208	const [billId, amountSen, paid = 'true'] = process.argv.slice(2)
209	const url = process.env.WEBHOOK_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway'
210	const key = process.env.GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY
211	
212	const myt = new Date(Date.now() + 8 _ 3600 _ 1000).toISOString()
213	const fields = {
214	id: billId,
215	paid,
216	paid_amount: paid === 'true' ? amountSen : '0',
217	paid_at: `${myt.slice(0, 10)} ${myt.slice(11, 19)} +0800`,
218	transaction_id: `TX-${Date.now()}`,
219	transaction_status: paid === 'true' ? 'completed' : 'failed',
220	}
221	const source = Object.keys(fields).sort().map(k => `${k}${fields[k]}`).join('|')
222	fields.x_signature = createHmac('sha256', key).update(source).digest('hex')
223	
224	const res = await fetch(url, {
225	method: 'POST',
226	headers: { 'content-type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
227	body: new URLSearchParams(fields),
228	})
229	console.log(res.status, await res.text())
230	
231	## 6. Access Control
232	
233	Access is enforced in two places, and we test both:
234	
235	- Your server code: route handlers, Server Actions and server components. Every endpoint must authenticate the caller and check their organization and role itself. A protected page or a hidden button is not a check.
236	- The Supabase Data API and Storage, which anyone holding your publishable key can call directly with their own access token.
237	
238	### Server code
239	
240	- Roles come from your memberships table, and from tenants.user_id for tenants. Never take a role or an organization from anything the user can edit, such as user_metadata.
241	- On the server, authenticate with supabase.auth.getUser() or getClaims(), not getSession().
242	- A request about a record in another organization, or another tenant's record, gets 404: do not reveal that it exists. A request about a record the caller can see, for an action their role does not allow, gets 403. A request without a valid login gets 401.
243	- IDs in request bodies are untrusted too. For example, a manager must not be able to create a lease on another organization's unit or tenant.
244	- Our tests call your API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, where the token is a Supabase access token for one of the seeded users. Accept that header as well as the normal session cookie.
245	- The service role (secret) key must never reach the browser.
246	
247	### Data API
248	
249	This table is the most access allowed through the Supabase Data API, which is PostgREST called with a user's token. Granting less is fine where your app does not need it, with one exception: the tenant portal reads the tenant's own data, and updates their phone number, directly from the browser with supabase-js.
250	Table | anon | tenant | staff | manager |
251	organizations | none | read own organization | read own organization | read own organization |
252	memberships | none | none | read own organization | read own organization |
253	units | none | read the units of own leases | read own organization | read own organization |
254	tenants | none | read own row, update only phone | read own organization | read own organization |
255	leases, invoices, payments, payment_allocations, gateway_bills | none | read the rows of own leases | read own organization | read own organization |
256	audit_log | none | none | none | read own organization |
257	
258	Every other insert, update or delete through the Data API must fail for everyone. This covers every table, view and function (/rest/v1/rpc/...) you create, not just the ones above. audit_log is append-only for every role, including the service role and the database owner.
259	
260	### Storage
261	
262	Bank transfer slips go in a private bucket named payment-slips, under <org_id>/.... Only staff and managers of that organization can upload there, and they read slips through short-lived signed URLs. Tenants, other organizations and anonymous users cannot read, list or upload slips. A payment's slip_path must point to an existing file in its own organization's folder.
263	
264	## 7. HTTP API
265	
266	Request and response bodies are JSON, except for the webhook. Amounts are integers in sen. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and instants are ISO 8601 with an offset. Errors return { "error": "message" }.
267	Method and path | Who | Success | Other responses |
268	POST /api/leases | manager | 201 { id } | 400 invalid input, 409 overlaps another lease on the unit |
269	GET /api/leases/:leaseId | staff, manager, the lease's tenant | 200, shape below | |
270	POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments | staff, manager | 201 { id, status } | 400 invalid input, 422 over the cap |
271	POST /api/payments/:paymentId/approve | manager | 200 { status } | 409 not pending, 422 over the remaining balance |
272	POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject | manager | 200 { status } | 400 missing reason, 409 not pending |
273	POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void | manager | 200 { status } | 400 missing reason, 409 not approved |
274	POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills | the lease's tenant | 201 { billId, amountSen } | 422 nothing due |
275	GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM | staff, manager | 200 [{ month: 'YYYY-MM', collectedSen }], one entry per month in order | 400 invalid range |
276	POST /api/webhooks/gateway | the gateway | see section 5 | |
277	
278	Every endpoint also returns 401, 403 and 404 as described in section 6. Request bodies:
279	// POST /api/leases
280	{ unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
281	
282	// POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments
283	{ amountSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer'; receivedAt: string; slipPath?: string }
284	
285	// POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject and POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void
286	{ reason: string }
287	GET /api/leases/:leaseId returns the invoices in allocation order:
288	{
289	lease: { id: string; unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
290	invoices: {
291	id: string; kind: 'deposit' | 'rent'; periodIndex: number | null; periodStart: string | null; periodEnd: string | null
292	dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number; status: InvoiceStatus
293	}[]
294	payments: {
295	id: string; amountSen: number; unappliedSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer' | 'online'
296	status: 'pending_verification' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'voided'; receivedAt: string
297	}[]
298	}
299	Creating a lease stores the lease and exactly the invoices generateSchedule returns, all or nothing. Leases on the same unit never overlap (both dates are inclusive), even when two requests arrive at the same moment.
300	
301	## 8. Database
302	
303	- Keep every database object in SQL migrations under supabase/migrations/: tables, constraints, RLS policies, grants, functions, triggers, and the storage bucket and its policies. npx supabase db reset must rebuild all of it; nothing may depend on changes made by hand in Supabase Studio. Use Prisma for server-side data access, with prisma/schema.prisma matching the database.
304	- Store money as integer sen (bigint), never as a floating-point type. Calendar dates are date, and instants are timestamptz.
305	- Required tables and columns (add whatever else you need):
306	  Table | Required columns |
307	  organizations | id, name |
308	  memberships | user_id, org_id, role (manager or staff) |
309	  units | id, org_id, name |
310	  tenants | id, org_id, user_id, full_name, email, phone |
311	  leases | id, org_id, unit_id, tenant_id, start_date, end_date, monthly_rent_sen, deposit_sen |
312	  invoices | id, org_id, lease_id, kind, period_index, period_start, period_end, due_date, amount_sen |
313	  payments | id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, unapplied_sen, method, status, received_at, slip_path, gateway_bill_id |
314	  payment_allocations | id, org_id, payment_id, invoice_id, amount_sen |
315	  gateway_bills | id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, status (pending, paid or failed) |
316	  audit_log | id, org_id, actor_id, action, entity_id, details, created_at |
317	
318	## 9. UI
319	
320	Use shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS throughout, with toasts for every action (success and error), loading states instead of blank screens, and helpful messages for empty and invalid input. TypeScript in strict mode, without any.
321	Staff and managers:
322	
323	- A dashboard with the number of overdue invoices and the collections report for the last 6 months.
324	- A list of leases, and a lease page with its invoices (period, due date, amount, paid, status) and payments (with a link to the slip for bank transfers).

# Technical Assessment - Rent Collection

Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router) - TypeScript - Supabase (Postgres, Auth, Storage) - Prisma - shadcn/ui - Tailwind CSS
Time: the timer above is what counts, normally 4 hours (about 30 min reading - 3 h building - 30 min write-ups and submission)

## Read This First

AI assistants (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot...) are allowed and expected. We assess whether you understand and control what gets built. Code you cannot explain counts as not done.

- Hidden tests. We run automated tests against every rule in this brief, including edge cases that are not in the examples:- your billing functions, about 50 hidden cases, run under TZ=UTC, TZ=Asia/Kuala_Lumpur and TZ=America/New_York
- your HTTP API, called as each seeded account, including requests about other organizations' records and concurrent requests
- your Supabase Data API and Storage bucket, called directly with your publishable key and each user's token
- your payment webhook, with valid, forged, duplicated, concurrent and out-of-order callbacks

- AI logs. Export the transcript of every AI session you use (in Claude Code: /export) into an ai-logs/ folder in your repo. We do not count how much you used AI. We look at how you directed it, what you checked and what you corrected.
- Walkthrough. If your submission passes, the interview starts with a 30-minute walkthrough of your code: we pick parts of it, ask "what happens if...", and ask you to make a small change live.
- Priorities. A correct and secure subset beats a complete but sloppy app. If time runs short, work in this order: billing functions (section 3), access control (6), payments (4), webhook (5), UI (9). Say in your README what you skipped.
- Names are a contract. Table names, column names, endpoint paths, file paths and response shapes in this brief are what our tests use. You may add more of your own.

## 1. The Business

You are building part of the rent collection module of a property management platform used by Malaysian property management companies.

- Each organization (a property management company) rents units to tenants under leases.
- A lease produces invoices: an optional deposit, plus one rent invoice per monthly period.
- Tenants pay by cash, by bank transfer (with an uploaded slip), or online through a payment gateway. Payments are allocated to invoices.
- Business timezone: Asia/Kuala_Lumpur (UTC+8, no daylight saving). Currency: MYR (RM). 1 ringgit = 100 sen.
- Your server runs in UTC and our assessors work from several timezones. Every date and time the app shows or accepts is Malaysia time, whatever the timezone of the server or of the viewer's device.

### Roles

Role | Who | Can |
manager | Organization admin | Everything in their organization: create leases, record payments (approved immediately), approve, reject and void payments, read the audit log |
staff | Front desk | Read their organization's leases, invoices and payments; record payments (these wait for a manager's approval) |
tenant | Renter | Read their own profile, leases, invoices and payments; update their own phone number; pay online |

A staff member or manager belongs to exactly one organization. Nobody ever sees another organization's data.

## 2. Local Setup and Seed Data

Develop against a local Supabase stack (Docker and the Supabase CLI), not a cloud project. See Supabase local development. We grade by running your project on our machine from a fresh clone, with exactly these commands:
npx supabase start # starts the stack from your supabase/config.toml
npx supabase db reset # rebuilds the database from supabase/migrations/
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local # we replace keys with the values from `npx supabase status` if they differ
npm run seed
npm run build && npm start

- Commit supabase/config.toml, supabase/migrations/, and an .env.example that lists every variable your app needs, with local values and a comment saying where each one comes from.
- npm run seed creates exactly the data below on a freshly reset database, through your normal code paths (your lease creation and payment logic), so the invoices and allocations it produces are the ones your app would produce.
- All seeded accounts share one password of your choice, which you submit with your work.

### Organizations and accounts

Organization | Account | Role | Notes |
Northwind Properties | manager@northwind.test | manager | |
Northwind Properties | staff@northwind.test | staff | |
Northwind Properties | aisyah@northwind.test | tenant | Tenant "Aisyah Rahman" |
Northwind Properties | ben@northwind.test | tenant | Tenant "Ben Lim" |
Northwind Properties | probe@northwind.test | tenant | Tenant "Probe Tenant" (our tests create payments and leases for this tenant) |
Beta Realty | manager@beta.test | manager | |
Beta Realty | chen@beta.test | tenant | Tenant "Chen Wei" |

### Units and leases

Organization | Unit | Tenant | Start | End | Monthly rent | Deposit |
Northwind | A-12-3 | Aisyah Rahman | 2026-01-31 | 2026-07-15 | RM 1,500.00 | RM 3,000.00 |
Northwind | B-05-1 | Ben Lim | 2026-01-01 | 2026-04-15 | RM 1,000.29 | none |
Northwind | C-01-7 | Probe Tenant | 2026-02-28 | 2027-02-27 | RM 2,000.00 | RM 4,000.00 |
Northwind | D-03-2 | (no lease) | | | | |
Beta | KL-1 | Chen Wei | 2026-03-15 | 2027-03-14 | RM 2,200.00 | RM 4,400.00 |

### Payments on Aisyah's lease

- Cash, RM 3,000.00, received 2026-01-31 10:00 Malaysia time, recorded by the manager.
- Bank transfer, RM 2,000.00, received 2026-03-01 00:30 Malaysia time, recorded by staff with a slip file, then approved by the manager.

## 3. Billing Rules - lib/billing.ts

Create lib/billing.ts (or src/lib/billing.ts). It must be pure: no I/O, no imports from Next.js, React, Supabase or Prisma, and no dependence on the timezone of the machine it runs on. Your app must use it, and we test it directly.
export type InvoiceKind = 'deposit' | 'rent'

export interface ScheduledInvoice {
kind: InvoiceKind
periodIndex: number | null // 0, 1, 2... for rent; null for the deposit
periodStart: string | null // 'YYYY-MM-DD'; null for the deposit
periodEnd: string | null // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive; null for the deposit
dueDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
amountSen: number // integer
}

export function generateSchedule(lease: {
startDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD'
endDate: string // 'YYYY-MM-DD', inclusive (the tenant's last day)
monthlyRentSen: number
depositSen: number
}): ScheduledInvoice[]

export type InvoiceStatus = 'paid' | 'partially_paid' | 'unpaid' | 'overdue'

export function invoiceStatus(
invoice: { dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number },
now: Date,
): InvoiceStatus

export function parseRinggitToSen(input: string): number

### generateSchedule

- Validation. Throw an Error if a date is not a real calendar date written as YYYY-MM-DD, if endDate is before startDate, if monthlyRentSen is not a positive integer, or if depositSen is not a non-negative integer.
- Deposit. If depositSen > 0, the first invoice is the deposit: kind: 'deposit', due on startDate, period fields null.
- Anchors. Rent periods are anchored on the start date. The anchor of period k is the start date plus k calendar months, always counted from the start date (never from the previous anchor). If that month has fewer days than the start day, use the month's last day. A lease starting on Jan 31 has anchors Jan 31, Feb 28 (Feb 29 in leap years), Mar 31, Apr 30, and so on.
- Periods. Period k runs from anchor k to the day before anchor k+1, and is due on anchor k. There is a period for every anchor on or before endDate.
- Last period. It is cut at endDate. If it is shorter than its full length, it costs monthlyRentSen x days used / days in the full period, rounded half up to the nearest sen. Every other period costs monthlyRentSen.
- Order. The deposit first, then rent by period index.
  Worked example (Aisyah's lease):
  Period | Kind | Dates | Due | Amount |
  | deposit | | 2026-01-31 | RM 3,000.00 |
  0 | rent | 2026-01-31 to 2026-02-27 | 2026-01-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
  1 | rent | 2026-02-28 to 2026-03-30 | 2026-02-28 | RM 1,500.00 |
  2 | rent | 2026-03-31 to 2026-04-29 | 2026-03-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
  3 | rent | 2026-04-30 to 2026-05-30 | 2026-04-30 | RM 1,500.00 |
  4 | rent | 2026-05-31 to 2026-06-29 | 2026-05-31 | RM 1,500.00 |
  5 | rent | 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-15 | 2026-06-30 | RM 774.19 |

Period 5 uses 16 of the 31 days from 2026-06-30 to 2026-07-30: 150000 x 16 / 31 = 77419.35, so 77419 sen.

### invoiceStatus

Apply these rules in order:

- paid if paidSen >= amountSen.
- overdue if today's Malaysia date is after dueDate. An invoice due 2026-03-01 becomes overdue at 2026-03-02 00:00 Malaysia time (2026-03-01T16:00:00Z), not a moment earlier.
- partially_paid if paidSen > 0.
- Otherwise unpaid.

### parseRinggitToSen

Turns what a user types into sen. It accepts digits with optional comma thousands separators (groups of exactly three digits) and an optional decimal part of one or two digits, ignoring whitespace around the value: "1,500.50" gives 150050, "1.15" gives 115, "7" gives 700. Anything else throws an Error, for example "", "-5", "1.234", "1e3", "RM 10", "1,23".

## 4. Payments

### Recording a payment

- Staff and managers record cash or bank transfer payments on a lease: the amount, the method, and the date and time the money was received (entered and shown in Malaysia time).
- A bank transfer needs a slip: a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB, stored in Supabase Storage (section 6). If recording fails after the upload, the file must not be left behind.
- A payment recorded by a manager is approved immediately. A payment recorded by staff is pending_verification until a manager approves or rejects it.
- Cap. A new payment may not be more than the lease's remaining balance (the total of all its invoices minus everything allocated to them) minus the total of the lease's payments still pending_verification. Paying future periods in advance is allowed within the cap.

### Approving, rejecting and voiding (managers only)

- Approve a pending_verification payment. At that moment, check again that it is not more than the lease's remaining balance. If it is, refuse and leave it pending.
- Reject a pending_verification payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters.
- Void an approved payment, with a reason of at least 5 characters. Voiding removes that payment's allocations. Other payments' allocations do not change.
- Payments are never deleted. Every approval, rejection, void and lease creation writes a row to audit_log (who, what, when, details).

### Allocation

When a payment becomes approved, its amount is allocated to the lease's invoices that still have something unpaid, in this order: due date, then deposit before rent, then period index. Each invoice is filled up to its unpaid amount before the next one, including invoices that are not due yet. Whatever is left once every invoice is fully paid is stored on the payment as unapplied_sen. Only online payments can end up with an unapplied amount, because manual payments are capped.
The paid amount of an invoice is the sum of its allocations. Statuses are computed with invoiceStatus, never stored.
All of this must stay correct when requests arrive at the same time. For example, two staff members recording payments on the same lease at once must not exceed the cap together, and a payment approved twice at once is allocated once.

### Collections report

The total of approved payments for each calendar month of received_at in Malaysia time, over a range of months, including months with nothing collected. With the seed data, Northwind's report for 2026-01 to 2026-03 is [{ month: '2026-01', collectedSen: 300000 }, { month: '2026-02', collectedSen: 0 }, { month: '2026-03', collectedSen: 200000 }].

## 5. Online Payments

A tenant pays online like this:

- The tenant clicks Pay now on their lease. Your API creates a gateway bill for the amount due now: the unpaid amounts of the lease's invoices due on or before today's Malaysia date. If nothing is due, refuse. Bill ids must be impossible to guess.
- In production the tenant would now be redirected to the gateway. In this test, show the bill id and amount: we play the gateway using the simulator below.
- The gateway calls your webhook, POST /api/webhooks/gateway. Only the webhook can settle a bill. The gateway also sends the tenant back to /payments/return?bill_id=...&paid=true. That page only shows the bill's real status from your database and changes nothing.

### Webhook

The request body is application/x-www-form-urlencoded, with these fields. The gateway may add more fields in future.
Field | Example | Notes |
id | bill_8f3a2c | Your bill id (this short example is guessable; yours must not be) |
paid | true | true or false |
paid_amount | 210050 | Amount in sen; 0 when not paid |
paid_at | 2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800 | When it was paid |
transaction_id | TX-000123 | Gateway transaction id |
transaction_status | completed | completed, failed or pending |
x_signature | 06994f... | See below |

Signature. Take every field in the request except x_signature, sort them by key (ascending by character code), write each one as the key immediately followed by the value, join them with |, and compute the HMAC-SHA256 of the resulting string with your secret key GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY, as lowercase hex. Test vector, with the key test_x_signature_key and the six example values above:
source: idbill_8f3a2c|paidtrue|paid_amount210050|paid_at2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800|transaction_idTX-000123|transaction_statuscompleted
signature: 06994fab2d674e7829144eaa2204631716d3c099b503d38945e92b6296531641
Required behavior:
Situation | Response | Effect |
Signature missing or wrong | 401 | None |
Unknown bill id | 404 | None |
paid=true and paid_amount is not the bill's amount | 422 | None |
paid=true, bill pending or failed | 200 | Bill becomes paid, and one approved online payment is created with received_at = paid_at, then allocated |
paid=true, bill already paid (a repeat delivery) | 200 | None |
paid=false, bill pending | 200 | Bill becomes failed |
paid=false, bill already failed (a repeat delivery) | 200 | None |
paid=false, bill already paid (late or out of order) | 200 | None: a paid bill never goes back |

The gateway retries, so it may deliver the same callback several times, including at the same moment. A bill creates at most one payment, ever. Never log the secret key or whole callback payloads.

### Simulator

Save this as gateway-sim.mjs and run node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> [true|false] with GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY set.
import { createHmac } from 'node:crypto'

const [billId, amountSen, paid = 'true'] = process.argv.slice(2)
const url = process.env.WEBHOOK_URL ?? 'http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway'
const key = process.env.GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY

const myt = new Date(Date.now() + 8 _ 3600 _ 1000).toISOString()
const fields = {
id: billId,
paid,
paid_amount: paid === 'true' ? amountSen : '0',
paid_at: `${myt.slice(0, 10)} ${myt.slice(11, 19)} +0800`,
transaction_id: `TX-${Date.now()}`,
transaction_status: paid === 'true' ? 'completed' : 'failed',
}
const source = Object.keys(fields).sort().map(k => `${k}${fields[k]}`).join('|')
fields.x_signature = createHmac('sha256', key).update(source).digest('hex')

const res = await fetch(url, {
method: 'POST',
headers: { 'content-type': 'application/x-www-form-urlencoded' },
body: new URLSearchParams(fields),
})
console.log(res.status, await res.text())

## 6. Access Control

Access is enforced in two places, and we test both:

- Your server code: route handlers, Server Actions and server components. Every endpoint must authenticate the caller and check their organization and role itself. A protected page or a hidden button is not a check.
- The Supabase Data API and Storage, which anyone holding your publishable key can call directly with their own access token.

### Server code

- Roles come from your memberships table, and from tenants.user_id for tenants. Never take a role or an organization from anything the user can edit, such as user_metadata.
- On the server, authenticate with supabase.auth.getUser() or getClaims(), not getSession().
- A request about a record in another organization, or another tenant's record, gets 404: do not reveal that it exists. A request about a record the caller can see, for an action their role does not allow, gets 403. A request without a valid login gets 401.
- IDs in request bodies are untrusted too. For example, a manager must not be able to create a lease on another organization's unit or tenant.
- Our tests call your API with Authorization: Bearer <access token>, where the token is a Supabase access token for one of the seeded users. Accept that header as well as the normal session cookie.
- The service role (secret) key must never reach the browser.

### Data API

This table is the most access allowed through the Supabase Data API, which is PostgREST called with a user's token. Granting less is fine where your app does not need it, with one exception: the tenant portal reads the tenant's own data, and updates their phone number, directly from the browser with supabase-js.
Table | anon | tenant | staff | manager |
organizations | none | read own organization | read own organization | read own organization |
memberships | none | none | read own organization | read own organization |
units | none | read the units of own leases | read own organization | read own organization |
tenants | none | read own row, update only phone | read own organization | read own organization |
leases, invoices, payments, payment_allocations, gateway_bills | none | read the rows of own leases | read own organization | read own organization |
audit_log | none | none | none | read own organization |

Every other insert, update or delete through the Data API must fail for everyone. This covers every table, view and function (/rest/v1/rpc/...) you create, not just the ones above. audit_log is append-only for every role, including the service role and the database owner.

### Storage

Bank transfer slips go in a private bucket named payment-slips, under <org_id>/.... Only staff and managers of that organization can upload there, and they read slips through short-lived signed URLs. Tenants, other organizations and anonymous users cannot read, list or upload slips. A payment's slip_path must point to an existing file in its own organization's folder.

## 7. HTTP API

Request and response bodies are JSON, except for the webhook. Amounts are integers in sen. Dates are YYYY-MM-DD, and instants are ISO 8601 with an offset. Errors return { "error": "message" }.
Method and path | Who | Success | Other responses |
POST /api/leases | manager | 201 { id } | 400 invalid input, 409 overlaps another lease on the unit |
GET /api/leases/:leaseId | staff, manager, the lease's tenant | 200, shape below | |
POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments | staff, manager | 201 { id, status } | 400 invalid input, 422 over the cap |
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/approve | manager | 200 { status } | 409 not pending, 422 over the remaining balance |
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject | manager | 200 { status } | 400 missing reason, 409 not pending |
POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void | manager | 200 { status } | 400 missing reason, 409 not approved |
POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills | the lease's tenant | 201 { billId, amountSen } | 422 nothing due |
GET /api/reports/collections?from=YYYY-MM&to=YYYY-MM | staff, manager | 200 [{ month: 'YYYY-MM', collectedSen }], one entry per month in order | 400 invalid range |
POST /api/webhooks/gateway | the gateway | see section 5 | |

Every endpoint also returns 401, 403 and 404 as described in section 6. Request bodies:
// POST /api/leases
{ unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }

// POST /api/leases/:leaseId/payments
{ amountSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer'; receivedAt: string; slipPath?: string }

// POST /api/payments/:paymentId/reject and POST /api/payments/:paymentId/void
{ reason: string }
GET /api/leases/:leaseId returns the invoices in allocation order:
{
lease: { id: string; unitId: string; tenantId: string; startDate: string; endDate: string; monthlyRentSen: number; depositSen: number }
invoices: {
id: string; kind: 'deposit' | 'rent'; periodIndex: number | null; periodStart: string | null; periodEnd: string | null
dueDate: string; amountSen: number; paidSen: number; status: InvoiceStatus
}[]
payments: {
id: string; amountSen: number; unappliedSen: number; method: 'cash' | 'bank_transfer' | 'online'
status: 'pending_verification' | 'approved' | 'rejected' | 'voided'; receivedAt: string
}[]
}
Creating a lease stores the lease and exactly the invoices generateSchedule returns, all or nothing. Leases on the same unit never overlap (both dates are inclusive), even when two requests arrive at the same moment.

## 8. Database

- Keep every database object in SQL migrations under supabase/migrations/: tables, constraints, RLS policies, grants, functions, triggers, and the storage bucket and its policies. npx supabase db reset must rebuild all of it; nothing may depend on changes made by hand in Supabase Studio. Use Prisma for server-side data access, with prisma/schema.prisma matching the database.
- Store money as integer sen (bigint), never as a floating-point type. Calendar dates are date, and instants are timestamptz.
- Required tables and columns (add whatever else you need):
  Table | Required columns |
  organizations | id, name |
  memberships | user_id, org_id, role (manager or staff) |
  units | id, org_id, name |
  tenants | id, org_id, user_id, full_name, email, phone |
  leases | id, org_id, unit_id, tenant_id, start_date, end_date, monthly_rent_sen, deposit_sen |
  invoices | id, org_id, lease_id, kind, period_index, period_start, period_end, due_date, amount_sen |
  payments | id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, unapplied_sen, method, status, received_at, slip_path, gateway_bill_id |
  payment_allocations | id, org_id, payment_id, invoice_id, amount_sen |
  gateway_bills | id, org_id, lease_id, amount_sen, status (pending, paid or failed) |
  audit_log | id, org_id, actor_id, action, entity_id, details, created_at |

## 9. UI

Use shadcn/ui and Tailwind CSS throughout, with toasts for every action (success and error), loading states instead of blank screens, and helpful messages for empty and invalid input. TypeScript in strict mode, without any.
Staff and managers:

- A dashboard with the number of overdue invoices and the collections report for the last 6 months.
- A list of leases, and a lease page with its invoices (period, due date, amount, paid, status) and payments (with a link to the slip for bank transfers).
- Recording a payment: the amount typed in ringgit and parsed with parseRinggitToSen, the date and time received in Malaysia time, and a slip upload for bank transfers.
- Managers approve or reject pending payments, and void approved ones (with a confirmation step and a reason).
  Tenants:
- Their lease, invoices with statuses, payments, and the amount due now.
- Pay now, which shows the new gateway bill, and the /payments/return page.
- Editing their phone number.
  Every date and time is shown in Malaysia time, whatever the viewer's timezone (we check with a different browser timezone), without hydration warnings.

Billing functions (hidden tests) | 15 |
Access control: server code, Data API, Storage | 25 |
Payments: allocation, cap, approval, void, concurrency | 15 |
Webhook: signature, idempotency, concurrency | 15 |
Timezones: overdue, collections, input and display | 10 |
Code review (Part B) | 5 |

UI and code quality | 10 |

I read all 390 lines of the brief, then CLAUDE.md and the scaffold. Nothing is written yet; this is the plan only.

# A. Database

**Migration files** (I recommend hand-writing them; see D3):
- `20261029000100_schema.sql`: extensions, enums, tables, constraints, audit trigger
- `20261029000200_rls_grants.sql`: helper functions, RLS, grants
- `20261029000300_storage.sql`: the bucket and its policies

## A1. Schema

```sql
-- Extension in `extensions`, NOT public: btree_gist adds ~100 functions; in public they'd be callable via /rest/v1/rpc.
create extension if not exists btree_gist with schema extensions;

create type public.membership_role     as enum ('manager','staff');
create type public.invoice_kind        as enum ('deposit','rent');
create type public.payment_method      as enum ('cash','bank_transfer','online');
create type public.payment_status      as enum ('pending_verification','approved','rejected','voided');
create type public.gateway_bill_status as enum ('pending','paid','failed');

create table public.organizations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null check (length(btrim(name)) > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table public.memberships (
  user_id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,   -- PK => exactly one org per staff/manager
  org_id  uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  role    public.membership_role not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index on public.memberships(org_id);

create table public.units (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  name text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (org_id, name),
  unique (id, org_id)                                   -- target for composite FKs
);

create table public.tenants (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  user_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null,
  full_name text not null,
  email text not null,
  phone text check (phone is null or phone ~ '^\+?[0-9][0-9 -]{6,19}$'),  -- browser writes this directly, so no Zod there
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (org_id, user_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.tenants(user_id);

create table public.leases (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  unit_id uuid not null,
  tenant_id uuid not null,
  start_date date not null,
  end_date date not null,
  monthly_rent_sen bigint not null check (monthly_rent_sen > 0),
  deposit_sen bigint not null check (deposit_sen >= 0),
  created_by uuid not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  check (end_date >= start_date),
  foreign key (unit_id, org_id)   references public.units(id, org_id),     -- DB refuses cross-org unit
  foreign key (tenant_id, org_id) references public.tenants(id, org_id),   -- DB refuses cross-org tenant
  unique (id, org_id),
  constraint leases_no_overlap exclude using gist
    (unit_id with =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') with &&)       -- 23P01 -> 409
);
create index on public.leases(org_id);
create index on public.leases(tenant_id);

create table public.invoices (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  kind public.invoice_kind not null,
  period_index int,
  period_start date,
  period_end date,
  due_date date not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen >= 0),   -- >= 0, not > 0: a 1-sen rent prorated over 1/31 rounds to 0
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  check (
    (kind = 'deposit' and period_index is null and period_start is null and period_end is null)
    or (kind = 'rent' and period_index >= 0 and period_start is not null and period_end >= period_start)
  ),
  unique (lease_id, period_index),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create unique index invoices_one_deposit on public.invoices(lease_id) where kind = 'deposit';
create index on public.invoices(lease_id, due_date);
create index on public.invoices(org_id, due_date);

create table public.gateway_bills (
  id text primary key check (id ~ '^bill_[0-9a-f]{32}$'),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  status public.gateway_bill_status not null default 'pending',
  transaction_id text,
  paid_at timestamptz,
  created_by uuid not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.gateway_bills(lease_id);

create table public.payments (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  unapplied_sen bigint not null default 0 check (unapplied_sen >= 0 and unapplied_sen <= amount_sen),
  method public.payment_method not null,
  status public.payment_status not null,
  received_at timestamptz not null,
  slip_path text unique,                                -- one slip, one payment (also makes orphan cleanup safe)
  gateway_bill_id text unique,                          -- a bill creates at most one payment, ever
  recorded_by uuid,                                     -- null for webhook
  reviewed_by uuid,
  reviewed_at timestamptz,
  review_reason text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  foreign key (gateway_bill_id, org_id) references public.gateway_bills(id, org_id),
  check ((method = 'bank_transfer') = (slip_path is not null)),
  check ((method = 'online') = (gateway_bill_id is not null)),
  check (slip_path is null or starts_with(slip_path, org_id::text || '/')),
  check (method <> 'online' or status in ('approved','voided')),
  check (status not in ('rejected','voided') or length(btrim(review_reason)) >= 5),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.payments(lease_id, status);
create index on public.payments(org_id, status, received_at);

create table public.payment_allocations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  payment_id uuid not null,
  invoice_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (payment_id, org_id) references public.payments(id, org_id),
  foreign key (invoice_id, org_id) references public.invoices(id, org_id),
  unique (payment_id, invoice_id)
);
create index on public.payment_allocations(invoice_id);
create index on public.payment_allocations(org_id);

create table public.audit_log (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  actor_id uuid,                                        -- null = gateway/system
  action text not null,                                 -- lease.created | payment.approved | payment.rejected | payment.voided
  entity_id text not null,                              -- text: holds uuids and bill ids
  details jsonb not null default '{}',
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index on public.audit_log(org_id, created_at desc);

create schema app;                                      -- not in config.toml [api].schemas => not reachable via REST/RPC
create function app.forbid_audit_change() returns trigger language plpgsql set search_path = '' as $$
begin raise exception 'audit_log is append-only' using errcode = '42501'; end $$;
create trigger audit_log_no_update_delete before update or delete on public.audit_log
  for each row execute function app.forbid_audit_change();
create trigger audit_log_no_truncate before truncate on public.audit_log
  for each statement execute function app.forbid_audit_change();   -- a row trigger does NOT cover TRUNCATE
```

## A2. Helper functions

All of them are `language sql stable security definer set search_path = ''`, in `app`:

| Function | Returns | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `app.member_org_id()` | uuid | `select org_id from public.memberships where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.member_role()` | membership_role | same, `role` |
| `app.tenant_ids()` | setof uuid | `select id from public.tenants where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_org_ids()` | setof uuid | `select org_id from public.tenants where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_lease_ids()` | setof uuid | leases join tenants on `t.user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_unit_ids()` | setof uuid | `unit_id` from the same join |

This splits your `current_org_id()` on purpose; see D2.

## A3. RLS

RLS is enabled on all 10 tables but not forced, so Prisma (the owner) still bypasses it. Every policy is `to authenticated`, and calls are wrapped as `(select app.f())` so each is evaluated once per statement. Where a row lists two predicates, they are OR'd into a single policy. The tenant UPDATE policy is the only write policy anywhere.

| Table | Role | Op | Predicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| organizations | staff, manager | SELECT | `id = app.member_org_id()` |
| organizations | tenant | SELECT | `id in (select app.tenant_org_ids())` |
| memberships | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| units | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| units | tenant | SELECT | `id in (select app.tenant_unit_ids())` |
| tenants | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| tenants | tenant | SELECT | `user_id = auth.uid()` |
| tenants | tenant | UPDATE | USING and WITH CHECK `user_id = auth.uid()`; only `phone` (column grant) |
| leases | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| leases | tenant | SELECT | `tenant_id in (select app.tenant_ids())` |
| invoices, payments, gateway_bills | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| invoices, payments, gateway_bills | tenant | SELECT | `lease_id in (select app.tenant_lease_ids())` |
| payment_allocations | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| payment_allocations | tenant | SELECT | `exists (select 1 from invoices i where i.id = invoice_id and i.lease_id in (select app.tenant_lease_ids()))` |
| audit_log | manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id() and app.member_role() = 'manager'` |
| everything | anon | any | no policy, no grant |
| everything | any | INSERT / DELETE, other UPDATEs | no policy, no grant |

A user who signed up with no membership and no tenant row gets null or an empty set from every helper, so they see nothing.

## A4. Grants

```sql
revoke all on all tables    in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all sequences in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on tables    from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on sequences from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on functions from public, anon, authenticated;

grant select on public.organizations, public.memberships, public.units, public.tenants, public.leases,
  public.invoices, public.payments, public.payment_allocations, public.gateway_bills, public.audit_log
  to authenticated;
grant update (phone) on public.tenants to authenticated;

-- The app never writes through PostgREST; close the service_role write path too.
revoke insert, update, delete, truncate on all tables in schema public from service_role;

revoke all on schema app from public;
grant usage on schema app to authenticated;              -- policies run as the caller, so it needs EXECUTE
revoke execute on all functions in schema app from public, anon;
grant execute on function app.member_org_id(), app.member_role(), app.tenant_ids(),
  app.tenant_org_ids(), app.tenant_lease_ids(), app.tenant_unit_ids() to authenticated;
```

## A5. Storage

```sql
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values ('payment-slips', 'payment-slips', false, 5242880,
        array['image/jpeg','image/png','application/pdf']);

create policy payment_slips_insert on storage.objects for insert to authenticated
  with check (bucket_id = 'payment-slips'
              and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select app.member_org_id())::text);
create policy payment_slips_select on storage.objects for select to authenticated
  using (bucket_id = 'payment-slips'
         and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select app.member_org_id())::text);
-- No UPDATE/DELETE policy: no overwrite (upsert), no user deletes. Server cleans orphans with the secret key.
```

Server-side slip check when a payment is recorded:
1. `slipPath` must start with `${caller.orgId}/`.
2. The object must exist: Prisma `$queryRaw` on `storage.objects`, checking bucket, name, `metadata->>'size'` ≤ 5 MB and `metadata->>'mimetype'` in the allowed list.
3. If recording fails for any reason after that, delete the object, but only if no payment references it. Because `slip_path` is UNIQUE, a request that reuses someone else's slip can never delete it.

# D. Contradictions and gaps

1. **CLAUDE.md contradicts your decisions and the brief.** It says:
   - roles come from a `profiles` table (the brief says memberships plus `tenants.user_id`);
   - manual payments have an `idempotency_key` and webhook events are deduped on `(provider, event_id)` (neither is in the brief, and its own "don't build what the spec didn't ask" rule rules them out);
   - payments lock the invoice with `FOR UPDATE` (your decision 8 locks the lease);
   - dates use "the property's IANA timezone" (the brief fixes Asia/Kuala_Lumpur).

   I'll edit CLAUDE.md to match your decisions in slice 0.
2. **Decision 6 has gaps.**
   - Revoking EXECUTE from `anon, authenticated` isn't enough: functions grant EXECUTE to `PUBLIC` by default, so it must be revoked from PUBLIC too.
   - btree_gist has to go in the `extensions` schema, or its functions become callable through `/rpc`.
   - Supabase's default privileges are set `for role postgres`, so the revoke has to name that role.
   - The audit trigger needs a TRUNCATE variant.
   - A single `current_org_id()` that also returns a tenant's org would let tenants upload slips under the storage policy. That's why A2 splits it into member and tenant helpers.
3. **Prisma workflow.** `migrate diff` can't express the exclusion constraint, the CHECKs, the extension schema or the composite FKs. I recommend hand-writing the SQL, then running `prisma db pull` after reset, so the schema matches the database by construction. This contradicts CLAUDE.md's "generate SQL with prisma migrate diff" rule.
4. **Dates and times.**
   - The API's `receivedAt` is "ISO 8601 with an offset". The API should reject values without one; `parseMalaysiaLocal` is only for the UI form. Responses use `+08:00`.
   - billing.ts should inline its MYT shift rather than import myt.ts, in case the graders import the file on its own.
   - `paid_at` (`2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800`) needs its own parser. A valid signature with a bad field gets 400; the brief's table doesn't say.
5. **Cap versus approval.** When recording, the cap is invoices − allocated − pending. When approving, the brief says only "remaining balance", so other pending payments are not subtracted.
   - Voiding leaves `unapplied_sen` on other payments as it is ("other payments' allocations do not change"), and DECISIONS.md will say so.
   - Lock order is lease → bill → invoices everywhere. The webhook reads `bill.lease_id` without a lock, locks the lease, then re-reads the bill `FOR UPDATE`.

# Build plan — Rent Collection

Status: draft for review. Nothing below is implemented yet.

# A. Database

**Migration files** (hand-written; see D3):
- `20261029000100_schema.sql`: extensions, enums, tables, constraints, audit trigger
- `20261029000200_rls_grants.sql`: helper functions, RLS, grants
- `20261029000300_storage.sql`: the bucket and its policies

## A1. Schema

```sql
-- Extension in `extensions`, NOT public: btree_gist adds ~100 functions; in public they'd be callable via /rest/v1/rpc.
create extension if not exists btree_gist with schema extensions;

create type public.membership_role     as enum ('manager','staff');
create type public.invoice_kind        as enum ('deposit','rent');
create type public.payment_method      as enum ('cash','bank_transfer','online');
create type public.payment_status      as enum ('pending_verification','approved','rejected','voided');
create type public.gateway_bill_status as enum ('pending','paid','failed');

create table public.organizations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null check (length(btrim(name)) > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table public.memberships (
  user_id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,   -- PK => exactly one org per staff/manager
  org_id  uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  role    public.membership_role not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index on public.memberships(org_id);

create table public.units (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  name text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (org_id, name),
  unique (id, org_id)                                   -- target for composite FKs
);

create table public.tenants (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  user_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null,
  full_name text not null,
  email text not null,
  phone text check (phone is null or phone ~ '^\+?[0-9][0-9 -]{6,19}$'),  -- browser writes this directly, so no Zod there
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (org_id, user_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.tenants(user_id);

create table public.leases (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  unit_id uuid not null,
  tenant_id uuid not null,
  start_date date not null,
  end_date date not null,
  monthly_rent_sen bigint not null check (monthly_rent_sen > 0),
  deposit_sen bigint not null check (deposit_sen >= 0),
  created_by uuid not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  check (end_date >= start_date),
  foreign key (unit_id, org_id)   references public.units(id, org_id),     -- DB refuses cross-org unit
  foreign key (tenant_id, org_id) references public.tenants(id, org_id),   -- DB refuses cross-org tenant
  unique (id, org_id),
  constraint leases_no_overlap exclude using gist
    (unit_id with =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') with &&)       -- 23P01 -> 409
);
create index on public.leases(org_id);
create index on public.leases(tenant_id);

create table public.invoices (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  kind public.invoice_kind not null,
  period_index int,
  period_start date,
  period_end date,
  due_date date not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen >= 0),   -- >= 0, not > 0: a 1-sen rent prorated over 1/31 rounds to 0
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  check (
    (kind = 'deposit' and period_index is null and period_start is null and period_end is null)
    or (kind = 'rent' and period_index >= 0 and period_start is not null and period_end >= period_start)
  ),
  unique (lease_id, period_index),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create unique index invoices_one_deposit on public.invoices(lease_id) where kind = 'deposit';
create index on public.invoices(lease_id, due_date);
create index on public.invoices(org_id, due_date);

create table public.gateway_bills (
  id text primary key check (id ~ '^bill_[0-9a-f]{32}$'),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  status public.gateway_bill_status not null default 'pending',
  transaction_id text,
  paid_at timestamptz,
  created_by uuid not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.gateway_bills(lease_id);

create table public.payments (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  unapplied_sen bigint not null default 0 check (unapplied_sen >= 0 and unapplied_sen <= amount_sen),
  method public.payment_method not null,
  status public.payment_status not null,
  received_at timestamptz not null,
  slip_path text unique,                                -- one slip, one payment (also makes orphan cleanup safe)
  gateway_bill_id text unique,                          -- a bill creates at most one payment, ever
  recorded_by uuid,                                     -- null for webhook
  reviewed_by uuid,
  reviewed_at timestamptz,
  review_reason text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  foreign key (gateway_bill_id, org_id) references public.gateway_bills(id, org_id),
  check ((method = 'bank_transfer') = (slip_path is not null)),
  check ((method = 'online') = (gateway_bill_id is not null)),
  check (slip_path is null or starts_with(slip_path, org_id::text || '/')),
  check (method <> 'online' or status in ('approved','voided')),
  check (status not in ('rejected','voided') or length(btrim(review_reason)) >= 5),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.payments(lease_id, status);
create index on public.payments(org_id, status, received_at);

create table public.payment_allocations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  payment_id uuid not null,
  invoice_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (payment_id, org_id) references public.payments(id, org_id),
  foreign key (invoice_id, org_id) references public.invoices(id, org_id),
  unique (payment_id, invoice_id)
);
create index on public.payment_allocations(invoice_id);
create index on public.payment_allocations(org_id);

create table public.audit_log (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  actor_id uuid,                                        -- null = gateway/system
  action text not null,                                 -- lease.created | payment.approved | payment.rejected | payment.voided
  entity_id text not null,                              -- text: holds uuids and bill ids
  details jsonb not null default '{}',
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index on public.audit_log(org_id, created_at desc);

create schema app;                                      -- not in config.toml [api].schemas => not reachable via REST/RPC
create function app.forbid_audit_change() returns trigger language plpgsql set search_path = '' as $$
begin raise exception 'audit_log is append-only' using errcode = '42501'; end $$;
create trigger audit_log_no_update_delete before update or delete on public.audit_log
  for each row execute function app.forbid_audit_change();
create trigger audit_log_no_truncate before truncate on public.audit_log
  for each statement execute function app.forbid_audit_change();   -- a row trigger does NOT cover TRUNCATE
```

## A2. Helper functions

All of them are `language sql stable security definer set search_path = ''`, in `app`:

| Function | Returns | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `app.member_org_id()` | uuid | `select org_id from public.memberships where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.member_role()` | membership_role | same, `role` |
| `app.tenant_ids()` | setof uuid | `select id from public.tenants where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_org_ids()` | setof uuid | `select org_id from public.tenants where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_lease_ids()` | setof uuid | leases join tenants on `t.user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_unit_ids()` | setof uuid | `unit_id` from the same join |

This splits the original single `current_org_id()` on purpose; see D2.

## A3. RLS

RLS is enabled on all 10 tables but not forced, so Prisma (the owner) still bypasses it. Every policy is `to authenticated`, and calls are wrapped as `(select app.f())` so each is evaluated once per statement. Where a row lists two predicates, they are OR'd into a single policy. The tenant UPDATE policy is the only write policy anywhere.

| Table | Role | Op | Predicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| organizations | staff, manager | SELECT | `id = app.member_org_id()` |
| organizations | tenant | SELECT | `id in (select app.tenant_org_ids())` |
| memberships | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| units | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| units | tenant | SELECT | `id in (select app.tenant_unit_ids())` |
| tenants | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| tenants | tenant | SELECT | `user_id = auth.uid()` |
| tenants | tenant | UPDATE | USING and WITH CHECK `user_id = auth.uid()`; only `phone` (column grant) |
| leases | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| leases | tenant | SELECT | `tenant_id in (select app.tenant_ids())` |
| invoices, payments, gateway_bills | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| invoices, payments, gateway_bills | tenant | SELECT | `lease_id in (select app.tenant_lease_ids())` |
| payment_allocations | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| payment_allocations | tenant | SELECT | `exists (select 1 from invoices i where i.id = invoice_id and i.lease_id in (select app.tenant_lease_ids()))` |
| audit_log | manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id() and app.member_role() = 'manager'` |
| everything | anon | any | no policy, no grant |
| everything | any | INSERT / DELETE, other UPDATEs | no policy, no grant |

A user who signed up with no membership and no tenant row gets null or an empty set from every helper, so they see nothing.

## A4. Grants

```sql
revoke all on all tables    in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all sequences in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on tables    from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on sequences from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on functions from public, anon, authenticated;

grant select on public.organizations, public.memberships, public.units, public.tenants, public.leases,
  public.invoices, public.payments, public.payment_allocations, public.gateway_bills, public.audit_log
  to authenticated;
grant update (phone) on public.tenants to authenticated;

-- The app never writes through PostgREST; close the service_role write path too.
revoke insert, update, delete, truncate on all tables in schema public from service_role;

revoke all on schema app from public;
grant usage on schema app to authenticated;              -- policies run as the caller, so it needs EXECUTE
revoke execute on all functions in schema app from public, anon;
grant execute on function app.member_org_id(), app.member_role(), app.tenant_ids(),
  app.tenant_org_ids(), app.tenant_lease_ids(), app.tenant_unit_ids() to authenticated;
```

## A5. Storage

```sql
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values ('payment-slips', 'payment-slips', false, 5242880,
        array['image/jpeg','image/png','application/pdf']);

create policy payment_slips_insert on storage.objects for insert to authenticated
  with check (bucket_id = 'payment-slips'
              and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select app.member_org_id())::text);
create policy payment_slips_select on storage.objects for select to authenticated
  using (bucket_id = 'payment-slips'

-- No UPDATE/DELETE policy: no overwrite (upsert), no user deletes. Server cleans orphans with the secret key.
```

Server-side slip check when a payment is recorded:
1. `slipPath` must start with `${caller.orgId}/`.
2. The object must exist: Prisma `$queryRaw` on `storage.objects`, checking bucket, name, `metadata->>'size'` ≤ 5 MB and `metadata->>'mimetype'` in the allowed list.
3. If recording fails for any reason after that, delete the object, but only if no payment references it. Because `slip_path` is UNIQUE, a request that reuses someone else's slip can never delete it.
