<system-reminder>
Codebase and user instructions are shown below. Be sure to adhere to these instructions. IMPORTANT: These instructions OVERRIDE any default behavior and you MUST follow them exactly as written.

Contents of E:\Tutorials\ezyfusion-rent-collection\CLAUDE.md (project instructions, checked into the codebase):

# Project rules

Rent collection system for property managers. Next.js 16 (App Router, TypeScript), Supabase local (Postgres, Auth, RLS), Prisma 7 with pg adapter, shadcn/ui, Tailwind, Vitest, npm (graders run npm install / npm run seed / npm run build && npm start).

## Non-negotiables
- Money is integer sen (`*_sen` bigint); currency MYR. No float arithmetic on money. Rounding happens only in `src/lib/billing.ts` (pure, tested directly by the graders).
- Due dates and billing periods are `date` columns. Timestamps are `timestamptz`. Date math uses the property's IANA timezone. Never mutate a `Date` with setMonth for billing periods.
- Every mutation checks authorization server-side from the `profiles` table and scopes by `organization_id`. Never trust role or org from the client.
- Payments are idempotent: unique `idempotency_key`; webhook events deduped by unique `(provider, event_id)`; webhook signature verified with a timing-safe compare before any processing.
- Payment application runs in one transaction with `SELECT ... FOR UPDATE` on the invoice.
- Zod validates every request body, query and env var. Amounts in the API are integers.
- One error helper maps domain errors to HTTP responses. No stack traces to clients.

## Stack rules
- Next.js 16: `proxy.ts` (not middleware.ts); `cookies()`, `headers()`, `params`, `searchParams` are awaited; route handlers in `app/api/**/route.ts`; webhook route reads raw body with `req.text()`.
- Supabase SSR client from `@supabase/ssr` for auth; service-role client only in server code, never in `NEXT_PUBLIC_*`.
- Migrations: `supabase/migrations/*.sql` is the single source of truth. Prisma schema is the model; generate SQL with `prisma migrate diff`. Never run `prisma migrate dev`. Hand-written SQL for RLS, triggers, constraints.
- Prisma pinned to 7.10.1 (`prisma`, `@prisma/client`, `@prisma/adapter-pg`).
- Seed: `npx supabase db reset` then `npm run seed` (tsx script: auth users via admin API, then domain data THROUGH the real service functions, as the brief requires). Deterministic.

## Working style
- Small slices. Each slice: plan, test for the edge case, implement, run `npm test`, summarise diff.
- No new dependencies without saying why in the response.
- Do not build what the spec did not ask for. If something seems needed but isn't in the spec, say so and stop.
- When unsure, ask one precise question instead of guessing.

## Commands
- `npm run dev` / `npm run build` / `npm run lint` / `npm run typecheck` / `npm test` / `npm run seed`
- `npx supabase start|stop|status` / `npx supabase db reset`

Read `docs/brief.md` in full first, then `CLAUDE.md`. The brief's table names, column names, endpoint paths, file paths and response shapes are a contract; hidden tests use them exactly.
Project state: Next 16.4.2 scaffold, Prisma 7.10.1 + @prisma/adapter-pg, @supabase/ssr, zod 4, vitest, shadcn v4, npm with package-lock. `supabase/config.toml` exists; `supabase/migrations/` is empty. No app code yet.
Decisions I have already made. Do not reopen them, but tell me if the brief contradicts one.

1. Priority order is the brief's: billing lib -> schema + RLS + storage -> auth helper + API (leases, payments, approve/reject/void, allocation) -> seed -> webhook + gateway bills -> collections report -> minimal UI -> REVIEW.md, DECISIONS.md, README, ai-logs. UI is last and skeletal if time is short.
2. `src/lib/billing.ts` is pure. Date math is done on (year, month, day) integers or `Date.UTC` only; never `new Date(string)` with local parsing, never local getters. Must pass the Aisyah worked example and the parseRinggitToSen vectors exactly.
3. One timezone helper module, `src/lib/myt.ts`: `todayInMalaysia(now: Date): string`, `parseMalaysiaLocal('YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm'): Date` (treat as +08:00), `formatMalaysia(date)`. Every "today" and every date<->instant conversion in the app goes through it. The collections report groups by `received_at AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur'` in SQL with `generate_series` so empty months appear.
4. Money: bigint sen in Postgres, `BigInt` in Prisma, `number` only at the JSON edge.
5. Prisma connects as the database owner, so RLS does not apply to it. Authorization for every route lives in one helper: `getCaller(req)` accepts `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or the session cookie, calls `supabase.auth.getUser()`, then loads role + org from `memberships` or `tenants.user_id` via Prisma. Never user_metadata. Rules: no valid login -> 401; record in another org or another tenant's record -> 404; visible record but role not allowed -> 403. IDs in bodies are checked against the caller's org.
6. RLS is the real wall for the Data API and Storage, exactly per the brief's matrix. Helper SQL functions `app.current_org_id()` and `app.current_tenant_id()` (SECURITY DEFINER, STABLE, reading memberships/tenants by `auth.uid()`), used in policies. `REVOKE ALL` from anon on everything. authenticated gets SELECT per matrix; tenants get `UPDATE (phone)` column grant on tenants with a policy `user_id = auth.uid()`. No INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE grants otherwise. audit_log: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger that raises, so even the owner cannot change it. Any function I create in `public` is `REVOKE EXECUTE FROM anon, authenticated` unless needed.
7. Storage: private bucket `payment-slips` created in a migration, policies on `storage.objects` for INSERT and SELECT restricted to staff/manager whose `app.current_org_id()::text = (storage.foldername(name))[1]`. Server issues short-lived signed URLs. Slip validation: JPEG/PNG/PDF, <= 5 MB; if the payment insert fails after upload, delete the object.
8. Concurrency: every payment mutation (record, approve, void, webhook settle) runs in one Prisma transaction that first does `SELECT id FROM leases WHERE id = $1 FOR UPDATE`, serialising per lease. Webhook also locks the `gateway_bills` row FOR UPDATE and `payments.gateway_bill_id` is UNIQUE. Lease overlap: `btree_gist` extension + `EXCLUDE USING gist (unit_id WITH =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') WITH &&)` on leases, mapped to 409. # Build plan — Rent Collection

Status: draft for review. Nothing below is implemented yet.

# A. Database

**Migration files** (hand-written; see D3):
- `20261029000100_schema.sql`: extensions, enums, tables, constraints, audit trigger
- `20261029000200_rls_grants.sql`: helper functions, RLS, grants
- `20261029000300_storage.sql`: the bucket and its policies

## A1. Schema

```sql
-- Extension in `extensions`, NOT public: btree_gist adds ~100 functions; in public they'd be callable via /rest/v1/rpc.
create extension if not exists btree_gist with schema extensions;

create type public.membership_role     as enum ('manager','staff');
create type public.invoice_kind        as enum ('deposit','rent');
create type public.payment_method      as enum ('cash','bank_transfer','online');
create type public.payment_status      as enum ('pending_verification','approved','rejected','voided');
create type public.gateway_bill_status as enum ('pending','paid','failed');

create table public.organizations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  name text not null check (length(btrim(name)) > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);

create table public.memberships (
  user_id uuid primary key references auth.users(id) on delete cascade,   -- PK => exactly one org per staff/manager
  org_id  uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  role    public.membership_role not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index on public.memberships(org_id);

create table public.units (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  name text not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (org_id, name),
  unique (id, org_id)                                   -- target for composite FKs
);

create table public.tenants (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  user_id uuid references auth.users(id) on delete set null,
  full_name text not null,
  email text not null,
  phone text check (phone is null or phone ~ '^\+?[0-9][0-9 -]{6,19}$'),  -- browser writes this directly, so no Zod there
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  unique (org_id, user_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.tenants(user_id);

create table public.leases (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  unit_id uuid not null,
  tenant_id uuid not null,
  start_date date not null,
  end_date date not null,
  monthly_rent_sen bigint not null check (monthly_rent_sen > 0),
  deposit_sen bigint not null check (deposit_sen >= 0),
  created_by uuid not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  check (end_date >= start_date),
  foreign key (unit_id, org_id)   references public.units(id, org_id),     -- DB refuses cross-org unit
  foreign key (tenant_id, org_id) references public.tenants(id, org_id),   -- DB refuses cross-org tenant
  unique (id, org_id),
  constraint leases_no_overlap exclude using gist
    (unit_id with =, daterange(start_date, end_date, '[]') with &&)       -- 23P01 -> 409
);
create index on public.leases(org_id);
create index on public.leases(tenant_id);

create table public.invoices (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  kind public.invoice_kind not null,
  period_index int,
  period_start date,
  period_end date,
  due_date date not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen >= 0),   -- >= 0, not > 0: a 1-sen rent prorated over 1/31 rounds to 0
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  check (
    (kind = 'deposit' and period_index is null and period_start is null and period_end is null)
    or (kind = 'rent' and period_index >= 0 and period_start is not null and period_end >= period_start)
  ),
  unique (lease_id, period_index),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create unique index invoices_one_deposit on public.invoices(lease_id) where kind = 'deposit';
create index on public.invoices(lease_id, due_date);
create index on public.invoices(org_id, due_date);

create table public.gateway_bills (
  id text primary key check (id ~ '^bill_[0-9a-f]{32}$'),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  status public.gateway_bill_status not null default 'pending',
  transaction_id text,
  paid_at timestamptz,
  created_by uuid not null,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  updated_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.gateway_bills(lease_id);

create table public.payments (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  lease_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  unapplied_sen bigint not null default 0 check (unapplied_sen >= 0 and unapplied_sen <= amount_sen),
  method public.payment_method not null,
  status public.payment_status not null,
  received_at timestamptz not null,
  slip_path text unique,                                -- one slip, one payment (also makes orphan cleanup safe)
  gateway_bill_id text unique,                          -- a bill creates at most one payment, ever
  recorded_by uuid,                                     -- null for webhook
  reviewed_by uuid,
  reviewed_at timestamptz,
  review_reason text,
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (lease_id, org_id) references public.leases(id, org_id),
  foreign key (gateway_bill_id, org_id) references public.gateway_bills(id, org_id),
  check ((method = 'bank_transfer') = (slip_path is not null)),
  check ((method = 'online') = (gateway_bill_id is not null)),
  check (slip_path is null or starts_with(slip_path, org_id::text || '/')),
  check (method <> 'online' or status in ('approved','voided')),
  check (status not in ('rejected','voided') or length(btrim(review_reason)) >= 5),
  unique (id, org_id)
);
create index on public.payments(lease_id, status);
create index on public.payments(org_id, status, received_at);

create table public.payment_allocations (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null,
  payment_id uuid not null,
  invoice_id uuid not null,
  amount_sen bigint not null check (amount_sen > 0),
  created_at timestamptz not null default now(),
  foreign key (payment_id, org_id) references public.payments(id, org_id),
  foreign key (invoice_id, org_id) references public.invoices(id, org_id),
  unique (payment_id, invoice_id)
);
create index on public.payment_allocations(invoice_id);
create index on public.payment_allocations(org_id);

create table public.audit_log (
  id uuid primary key default gen_random_uuid(),
  org_id uuid not null references public.organizations(id),
  actor_id uuid,                                        -- null = gateway/system
  action text not null,                                 -- lease.created | payment.approved | payment.rejected | payment.voided
  entity_id text not null,                              -- text: holds uuids and bill ids
  details jsonb not null default '{}',
  created_at timestamptz not null default now()
);
create index on public.audit_log(org_id, created_at desc);

create schema app;                                      -- not in config.toml [api].schemas => not reachable via REST/RPC
create function app.forbid_audit_change() returns trigger language plpgsql set search_path = '' as $$
begin raise exception 'audit_log is append-only' using errcode = '42501'; end $$;
create trigger audit_log_no_update_delete before update or delete on public.audit_log
  for each row execute function app.forbid_audit_change();
create trigger audit_log_no_truncate before truncate on public.audit_log
  for each statement execute function app.forbid_audit_change();   -- a row trigger does NOT cover TRUNCATE
```

## A2. Helper functions

All of them are `language sql stable security definer set search_path = ''`, in `app`:

| Function | Returns | Body |
|---|---|---|
| `app.member_org_id()` | uuid | `select org_id from public.memberships where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.member_role()` | membership_role | same, `role` |
| `app.tenant_ids()` | setof uuid | `select id from public.tenants where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_org_ids()` | setof uuid | `select org_id from public.tenants where user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_lease_ids()` | setof uuid | leases join tenants on `t.user_id = auth.uid()` |
| `app.tenant_unit_ids()` | setof uuid | `unit_id` from the same join |

This splits the original single `current_org_id()` on purpose; see D2.

## A3. RLS

RLS is enabled on all 10 tables but not forced, so Prisma (the owner) still bypasses it. Every policy is `to authenticated`, and calls are wrapped as `(select app.f())` so each is evaluated once per statement. Where a row lists two predicates, they are OR'd into a single policy. The tenant UPDATE policy is the only write policy anywhere.

| Table | Role | Op | Predicate |
|---|---|---|---|
| organizations | staff, manager | SELECT | `id = app.member_org_id()` |
| organizations | tenant | SELECT | `id in (select app.tenant_org_ids())` |
| memberships | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| units | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| units | tenant | SELECT | `id in (select app.tenant_unit_ids())` |
| tenants | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| tenants | tenant | SELECT | `user_id = auth.uid()` |
| tenants | tenant | UPDATE | USING and WITH CHECK `user_id = auth.uid()`; only `phone` (column grant) |
| leases | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| leases | tenant | SELECT | `tenant_id in (select app.tenant_ids())` |
| invoices, payments, gateway_bills | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| invoices, payments, gateway_bills | tenant | SELECT | `lease_id in (select app.tenant_lease_ids())` |
| payment_allocations | staff, manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id()` |
| payment_allocations | tenant | SELECT | `exists (select 1 from invoices i where i.id = invoice_id and i.lease_id in (select app.tenant_lease_ids()))` |
| audit_log | manager | SELECT | `org_id = app.member_org_id() and app.member_role() = 'manager'` |
| everything | anon | any | no policy, no grant |
| everything | any | INSERT / DELETE, other UPDATEs | no policy, no grant |

A user who signed up with no membership and no tenant row gets null or an empty set from every helper, so they see nothing.

## A4. Grants

```sql
revoke all on all tables    in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all sequences in schema public from anon, authenticated;
revoke all on all functions in schema public from public, anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on tables    from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on sequences from anon, authenticated;
alter default privileges for role postgres in schema public revoke all on functions from public, anon, authenticated;

grant select on public.organizations, public.memberships, public.units, public.tenants, public.leases,
  public.invoices, public.payments, public.payment_allocations, public.gateway_bills, public.audit_log
  to authenticated;
grant update (phone) on public.tenants to authenticated;

-- The app never writes through PostgREST; close the service_role write path too.
revoke insert, update, delete, truncate on all tables in schema public from service_role;

revoke all on schema app from public;
grant usage on schema app to authenticated;              -- policies run as the caller, so it needs EXECUTE
revoke execute on all functions in schema app from public, anon;
grant execute on function app.member_org_id(), app.member_role(), app.tenant_ids(),
  app.tenant_org_ids(), app.tenant_lease_ids(), app.tenant_unit_ids() to authenticated;
```

## A5. Storage

```sql
insert into storage.buckets (id, name, public, file_size_limit, allowed_mime_types)
values ('payment-slips', 'payment-slips', false, 5242880,
        array['image/jpeg','image/png','application/pdf']);

create policy payment_slips_insert on storage.objects for insert to authenticated
  with check (bucket_id = 'payment-slips'
              and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select app.member_org_id())::text);
create policy payment_slips_select on storage.objects for select to authenticated
  using (bucket_id = 'payment-slips'
         and (storage.foldername(name))[1] = (select app.member_org_id())::text);
-- No UPDATE/DELETE policy: no overwrite (upsert), no user deletes. Server cleans orphans with the secret key.
```

Server-side slip check when a payment is recorded:
1. `slipPath` must start with `${caller.orgId}/`.
2. The object must exist: Prisma `$queryRaw` on `storage.objects`, checking bucket, name, `metadata->>'size'` ≤ 5 MB and `metadata->>'mimetype'` in the allowed list.
3. If recording fails for any reason after that, delete the object, but only if no payment references it. Because `slip_path` is UNIQUE, a request that reuses someone else's slip can never delete it.

# B. File layout

```
prisma.config.ts                      Prisma 7 config; must not throw when DATABASE_URL is unset (see D7)
prisma/schema.prisma                  generator "prisma-client" -> src/generated/prisma (git-ignored, postinstall)
supabase/migrations/2026102900{0100,0200,0300}_*.sql
.env.example                          6 vars + comment each
gateway-sim.mjs                       verbatim from the brief
scripts/seed.ts
src/proxy.ts                          session refresh only; no authz here
src/lib/billing.ts                    pure, self-contained (no import of myt.ts, see D4)
src/lib/billing.test.ts
src/lib/myt.ts                        todayInMalaysia, parseMalaysiaLocal, formatMalaysia, toMalaysiaIso, parseGatewayPaidAt
src/lib/myt.test.ts
src/lib/env.ts                        zod-parsed env, server-only
src/lib/http.ts                       DomainError(kind) -> status; json(); handle(fn) wrapper; maps 23P01/23505/P2028
src/lib/validation.ts                 zod schemas for every body/query
src/lib/gateway/signature.ts          pure sign/verify (timingSafeEqual, length check first)
src/lib/gateway/signature.test.ts     brief's test vector
src/lib/db/prisma.ts                  PrismaPg adapter singleton; tx options maxWait/timeout raised
src/lib/supabase/server.ts            createServerClient (cookies)
src/lib/supabase/browser.ts           createBrowserClient (publishable key)
src/lib/supabase/admin.ts             secret key; `import 'server-only'`
src/lib/auth/getCaller.ts             getCaller(req) -> userId -> loadCaller(userId) {userId, kind: manager|staff|tenant, orgId, tenantIds}
src/services/leases.ts                createLease(caller, input), getLease(caller, id)
src/services/allocation.ts            planAllocation(invoices, amount) pure + allocate(tx, paymentId)
src/services/allocation.test.ts
src/services/payments.ts              recordPayment, approvePayment, rejectPayment, voidPayment, lockLease(tx, id)
src/services/gatewayBills.ts          createGatewayBill, settleFromWebhook
src/services/reports.ts               collections(caller, from, to)
src/services/audit.ts                 writeAudit(tx, ...)
src/app/api/leases/route.ts                                  POST
src/app/api/leases/[leaseId]/route.ts                        GET
src/app/api/leases/[leaseId]/payments/route.ts               POST
src/app/api/leases/[leaseId]/gateway-bills/route.ts          POST
src/app/api/payments/[paymentId]/{approve,reject,void}/route.ts
src/app/api/reports/collections/route.ts                     GET
src/app/api/webhooks/gateway/route.ts                        POST (req.text())
src/app/login/page.tsx
src/app/(staff)/dashboard/page.tsx, leases/page.tsx, leases/[leaseId]/page.tsx (+ client forms)
src/app/(tenant)/portal/page.tsx      reads and phone update via supabase-js in the browser
src/app/payments/return/page.tsx      read-only bill status

- Services take a `Caller`. Routes only do `getCaller → zod → service → json`. The seed calls `loadCaller(userId)` and then the same services.
- UI mutations `fetch` the route handlers rather than going through Server Actions, so there is only one auth path.

# C. Slice order (160 min of building)

| # | Slice | Min | Done when |
|---|---|---|---|
| 0 | Scaffold fixes (D6) | 5 | `npm install` makes package-lock; `.env.example` tracked |
| 1 | billing.ts, myt.ts, signature.ts + tests (Aisyah, Ben's 50014.5→50015, Jan 31 anchors, leap year, parse vectors, the 16:00Z boundary, TZ loop) | 18 | `npm test` green |
| 2 | 3 migrations, `db reset`, schema.prisma, generate, env.ts, prisma.ts | 30 | reset is clean; prisma typechecks |
| 3 | supabase clients, getCaller/loadCaller, http.ts, proxy.ts | 12 | 401/403/404 helpers usable |
| 4 | leases service + POST/GET routes + audit | 12 | overlap → 409; foreign unit → 404 |
| 5 | allocation (pure + test), record (cap, slip), approve/reject/void | 28 | allocation test green |
| 6 | seed + verification: curl the Data API and Storage as anon/tenant/staff, check Aisyah's invoices and the report | 15 | report = 300000/0/200000 |
| 7 | gateway bills + webhook + gateway-sim.mjs; 2 concurrent sim calls → 1 payment | 18 | |
| 8 | collections report (`generate_series`, MYT grouping) | 7 | |
| 9 | Skeletal UI: login, dashboard, leases list and page, record/approve/void dialogs, tenant portal, return page | 15 | |

Writing time (30 min): REVIEW.md about 12, DECISIONS.md about 10, README and ai-logs about 8.

UI only gets 15 minutes. If anything runs over, UI is what shrinks, which matches the brief's priority order.

# D. Contradictions and gaps

1. **CLAUDE.md contradicts the decisions and the brief.** It says:
   - roles come from a `profiles` table (the brief says memberships plus `tenants.user_id`);
   - manual payments have an `idempotency_key` and webhook events are deduped on `(provider, event_id)` (neither is in the brief, and its own "don't build what the spec didn't ask" rule rules them out);
   - payments lock the invoice with `FOR UPDATE` (decision 8 locks the lease);
   - dates use "the property's IANA timezone" (the brief fixes Asia/Kuala_Lumpur).

   Edit CLAUDE.md to match the decisions in slice 0.
2. **Decision 6 has gaps.**
   - Revoking EXECUTE from `anon, authenticated` isn't enough: functions grant EXECUTE to `PUBLIC` by default, so it must be revoked from PUBLIC too.
   - btree_gist has to go in the `extensions` schema, or its functions become callable through `/rpc`.
   - Supabase's default privileges are set `for role postgres`, so the revoke has to name that role.
   - The audit trigger needs a TRUNCATE variant.
   - A single `current_org_id()` that also returns a tenant's org would let tenants upload slips under the storage policy. That's why A2 splits it into member and tenant helpers.
3. **Prisma workflow.** `migrate diff` can't express the exclusion constraint, the CHECKs, the extension schema or the composite FKs. Recommendation: hand-write the SQL, then run `prisma db pull` after reset, so the schema matches the database by construction. This contradicts CLAUDE.md's "generate SQL with prisma migrate diff" rule.
4. **Dates and times.**
   - The API's `receivedAt` is "ISO 8601 with an offset". The API should reject values without one; `parseMalaysiaLocal` is only for the UI form. Responses use `+08:00`.
   - billing.ts should inline its MYT shift rather than import myt.ts, in case the graders import the file on its own.
   - `paid_at` (`2026-04-01 00:30:12 +0800`) needs its own parser. A valid signature with a bad field gets 400; the brief's table doesn't say.
5. **Cap versus approval.** When recording, the cap is invoices − allocated − pending. When approving, the brief says only "remaining balance", so other pending payments are not subtracted.
   - Voiding leaves `unapplied_sen` on other payments as it is ("other payments' allocations do not change"), and DECISIONS.md will say so.
   - Lock order is lease → bill → invoices everywhere. The webhook reads `bill.lease_id` without a lock, locks the lease, then re-reads the bill `FOR UPDATE`.
   - Prisma's default transaction maxWait/timeout (2s/5s) will make concurrent tests fail with P2028, so raise them.
6. **The scaffold isn't as described.**
   - There is no package-lock.json.
   - `.gitignore` has `.env*`, which ignores `.env.example`; it needs `!.env.example`.
   - `src/lib/utils.ts` exports `cn` from the npm package `cn`. That isn't shadcn's clsx + tailwind-merge, so Tailwind class conflicts won't merge. Add `tailwind-merge` (clsx is already in node_modules), save both as explicit dependencies, and drop the `cn` package.
   - `next.config.ts` still has `cacheComponents: true` and `partialPrefetching`.
7. **Environment loading.** Graders run `npm install` before `cp .env.example .env.local`.
   - `postinstall: prisma generate` can't need `DATABASE_URL`.
   - Prisma 7 and tsx don't read `.env.local`, so the seed has to be `tsx --env-file=.env.local scripts/seed.ts`.
8. **Missed in the decisions.**
   - The brief requires the tenant portal to read its data and update the phone number through supabase-js in the browser.
   - `config.toml` has `enable_signup = true`, so anyone with the publishable key can create users. Set it to false; the admin API still works.
   - `invoices.amount_sen` has to allow 0.
   - The check order for every route is 401 → 404 → 403 → 400 → 409/422.
   - Ben's lease is a useful hidden-test vector: 100029 × 15/30 = 50014.5, which must round to 50015.
9. **A choice the brief leaves open.** When a manager sends `POST /api/leases` with another org's `unitId` or `tenantId`, return 404 rather than 400, because it doesn't reveal that the record exists.

New dependency proposed: `tailwind-merge` (reason in D6). Nothing else.

## Working style
- Small slices. Each slice: plan, test for the edge case, implement, run `npm test`, summarise diff, commit.

- Do not build what the spec did not ask for. If something seems needed but isn't in the spec, say so and stop.

---
title: proxy.js
description: API reference for the proxy.js file.
related:
  title: Learn more about Proxy
  links:
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-request
    - app/api-reference/functions/next-response
---
> **Note**: The `middleware` file convention is deprecated and has been renamed to `proxy`. See [Migration to Proxy](#migration-to-proxy) for more details.
The `proxy.js|ts` file is used to write [Proxy](/docs/app/getting-started/proxy) and run code on the server before a request is completed. Then, based on the incoming request, you can modify the response by rewriting, redirecting, modifying the request or response headers, or responding directly.
Proxy executes before routes are rendered. It's particularly useful for implementing custom server-side logic like authentication, logging, or handling redirects.
> **Good to know**:
>
> Proxy is meant to be invoked separately of your render code and in optimized cases deployed to your CDN for fast redirect/rewrite handling, you should not attempt relying on shared modules or globals.
>
> To pass information from Proxy to your application, use [headers](#setting-headers), [cookies](#using-cookies), [rewrites](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#rewrite), [redirects](/docs/app/api-reference/functions/next-response#redirect), or the URL.
Create a `proxy.ts` (or `.js`) file in the project root, or inside `src` if applicable, so that it is located at the same level as `pages` or `app`.
If you’ve customized [`pageExtensions`](/docs/app/api-reference/config/next-config-js/pageExtensions), for example to `.page.ts` or `.page.js`, name your file `proxy.page.ts` or `proxy.page.js` accordingly.
```tsx filename="proxy.ts" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
import type { NextRequest } from 'next/server'
// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request: NextRequest) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}
export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```
```js filename="proxy.js" switcher
import { NextResponse } from 'next/server'
// This function can be marked `async` if using `await` inside
export function proxy(request) {
  return NextResponse.redirect(new URL('/home', request.url))
}
export const config = {
  matcher: '/about/:path*',
}
```
## Exports
### Proxy function
The file must export a single function, either as a default export or named `proxy`. Note that multiple proxy from the same file are not supported.
```js filename="proxy.js"
// Example of default export
export default function proxy(request) {
  // Proxy logic
}
```
### Config object (optional)
Optionally, a config object can be exported alongside the Proxy function. This object includes the [matcher](#matcher) to specify paths where the Proxy applies.
### Matcher
The `matcher` option allows you to target specific paths for the Proxy to run on.
Without a `matcher`, Proxy runs on **every request**, including static files (`_next/static`), image optimizations (`_next/image`), and assets in the `public/` folder. Consider using a [negative match pattern](#negative-matching) to exclude these paths, otherwise auth logic or redirects can unintentionally block CSS, JS, or images from loading.
You can specify paths in several ways:
- For a single path: Directly use a string to define the path, like `'/about'`.
- For multiple paths: Use an array to list multiple paths, such as `matcher: ['/about', '/contact']`, which applies the Proxy to both `/about` and `/contact`.

Base directory for this skill: C:\Users\hp\.claude\skills\frontend-design

# Frontend Design

Approach this as the design lead at a design studio known for giving every client a distinct visual identity that is not mistaken for anyone else's. This client has already rejected proposals that felt cliché or templated, and is paying for a distinctive point of view: make deliberate, opinionated choices about palette, typography, and layout that are specific to this brief, and take aesthetic risk if justified.

## Ground your designs in the subject matter

If the brief does not identify what the product or subject matter is, identify it yourself before designing, and confirm with the client. You can come up with one concrete subject, the design's audience, and the design's primary job, as a proposal. If there's any information in your memory about the client's preferences or context about what they're building, use that as a hint. The subject's industry, subject matter, materials, and vernacular are where distinctive visual choices come from — a design for a toy for girls aged 8–11 will be very aesthetically different from a dashboard for financial analysts. Build with the brief's real content and subject matter throughout.

## Design principles

For web designs, the hero is the first thing viewers will see. Open with the most characteristic thing in the subject's world, in the form that is most appropriate: a headline, an image, an animation, a live demo, an interactive moment, or other treatments. Be deliberate with your choice: a big number with a small label, supporting stats, and a gradient accent is the default treatment, so only use it if that's truly the best option.

Typography carries the personality of the page. You don't need a different typeface for display or headline text and body content: use one family or two, and if two, make them clearly distinct.

Choose your typefaces deliberately, not the default families you would reach for on any other project, and set a clear type scale following the default guidance of The Elements of Typographic Style with intentional weights, widths, and spacing. When type is used as a headline or visual element, use the type treatment itself as an active part of the design, not a neutral delivery vehicle for the content.

Default to line lengths of less than 80 characters. Serif typefaces can have slightly longer line lengths; give serif body text slightly more line-height than a sans-serif.

Avoid these default typographic treatments; they are the commonest tells of a generated page:
- Accenting just a single word or phrase in a headline, like putting one word in italic/bold or a different color.
- Using all caps for labels.
- Adding unnecessary typographic labels above content.

Visual structure is information. Structural devices like outlines, borders, numbering, eyebrows, dividers, labels, etc., encode useful information about the content rather than decorate it. Many generic designs use numbered markers (01 / 02 / 03), but that's only appropriate if the content actually is a sequence — like a stepped process or a timeline. Before adding numbered markers, check the content really is a sequence.

Use non-user-triggered motion sparingly and deliberately, only to draw attention. A single orchestrated moment — one page-load sequence or one reveal — lands better than scattered effects; fade-and-slide-up entrances on each section and hover transitions on every card are the generic default and read as AI-generated. Motion that answers a person's action (opening, expanding, confirming) is welcome when it shows what changed.

Consider written content carefully. Often a design brief may not contain real content, and it's up to you to come up with copy and placeholder content. Copy can make a design feel as templated as the design itself. See the below section on writing for more guidance.

## Process: plan, review against the brief, build, critique

For calibration, AI-generated design right now clusters around some traits:
1. a warm cream background (near #F4F1EA) with a high-contrast serif display and a terracotta or warm-clay accent (often near #D97757 — Anthropic's own Claude-interaction accent, so on a user's brief it reads as a tell);
2. a near-black background with a single bright acid-green or vermilion accent;
3. a broadsheet-style layout with hairline rules, zero border-radius, and dense newspaper-like columns;
4. the SaaS-card kit: content chopped into identical rounded cards, one border-radius on everything regardless of hierarchy, the same soft grey shadow (rgba(0,0,0,.1)) under each, and gradient washes as decoration;
5. template chrome that appears whatever the subject: a tracked-out ALL-CAPS eyebrow label above every heading; meta strings joined with middle dots ('A · B · C'); labels built as 'WORD — fragment' with a spaced em dash; tinted near-black (#0B0B0B, #111) standing in for black; a monospace face for small data labels; a '→' appended to link and button text.

All traits are legitimate for some briefs, but they are defaults rather than choices, and they appear regardless of subject. Where the brief pins down a visual direction, follow it exactly — the brief's own words always win, including when it asks for one of these looks. Where it leaves an axis free, don't spend that freedom on one of these defaults. As with a hired human designer, there's often a careful balance between doing what you're good at and taking each project as a chance to experiment and learn.

Work in two passes. First, brainstorm a short design plan based on the client's design brief: create a compact token system with color, type, layout, and principles.
- Color: describe the core base palette as 4–6 named hex values.
- Type: the typefaces and their roles.
- Layout: a layout concept, using one-sentence prose descriptions and ASCII wireframes to ideate and compare. Include alignment guidance; should the content be left aligned, center aligned, justified?
- Principles: the high-level guidance for what makes this page unique.

Then review that plan against the brief before building: if any part of it reads like the generic default you would produce for any similar page (work through a similar prompt to see if you arrive somewhere similar) rather than a choice made for this specific brief — revise that part, say what you changed and why. Only after you've confirmed the relative uniqueness of your design plan should you start to write the code, following the revised plan.

When writing the code, be careful of structuring your CSS selector specificities. It's easy to generate CSS classes that cancel each other out (especially with a type-based selector like .section and an element-based selector like .cta). This can happen often with padding/margin between sections.

## Restraint and self-critique

Spend your boldness in one place. Let one element be the memorable thing, keep everything around it quiet and disciplined, and cut any decoration that does not serve the brief. Build to a quality floor without announcing it: responsive down to mobile, visible keyboard focus, reduced motion respected, visually accessible, harmonious color palettes. Critique your own work as you build, taking screenshots to review if your environment supports it — a picture is worth 1000 tokens. Consider Chanel's advice: before leaving the house, take a look in the mirror and remove one accessory. Human creatives have memory and always try to do something new, so if you have a space to quickly jot down notes about what you've tried, it can help you in future passes.

## More on writing in design

Words appear in a design for one reason: to make it easier to understand and use. They are design content, not decoration. Bring the same intentionality and minimalism to copywriting that you would bring to spacing and color. Before writing anything, ask what the design needs to say, and how it can best be said to help the person navigate the experience.

Write from the end user's perspective. Name things by what users will understand in simple language, not by how the system is built. A user manages notifications, not webhook config. Describe what something is or does in plain terms rather than selling it. Being specific and legible to new users is always better than being clever.

Use active voice as default. A CTA says exactly what happens when it is used: "Save changes," not "Submit." An action keeps the same name through the whole flow, so the button that says "Publish" produces a toast that says "Published." The vocabulary of an interface is the signposting for someone navigating the product. Cohesion and consistency are how people learn their way around.

Treat failure and emptiness as moments for direction, not mood. Explain what went wrong and how to fix it, in the interface's voice rather than a person's. Errors don't apologize, and they are never vague about what happened. An empty screen is an invitation to act.

Keep the tone conversational: plain verbs, sentence case, no filler, with tone matched to the brand and the audience. Let each written element do exactly one job.

input.content:
# Rent collection

Rent collection for Malaysian property management companies: leases produce a deposit and monthly rent invoices, and tenants pay by cash, bank transfer (with a slip) or online through a payment gateway. Staff record payments, managers approve, reject and void them, and tenants see their own lease and pay online.

Stack: Next.js 16 (App Router), TypeScript (strict), Supabase local (Postgres, Auth, Storage), Prisma 7 with the pg adapter, shadcn/ui, Tailwind CSS, Vitest. Business timezone Asia/Kuala_Lumpur, currency MYR.

## Run it

Needs Docker and Node 24 (npm 11). From a fresh clone, exactly as the brief's section 2:

```bash
npx supabase start          # starts the stack from supabase/config.toml
npx supabase db reset       # rebuilds the database from supabase/migrations/
npm install                 # also runs prisma generate
cp .env.example .env.local  # replace keys with `npx supabase status` values if they differ
npm run seed
npm run build && npm start  # http://localhost:3000
```

`npm run seed` only runs on a freshly reset database; it refuses otherwise. To start over: `npx supabase db reset && npm run seed`.

### Environment

All six variables are in `.env.example` with local values and a comment saying where each comes from.

| Variable | Where it comes from |
|---|---|
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL` | `API_URL` in `npx supabase status` |
| `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` | `PUBLISHABLE_KEY` in `npx supabase status` (safe in the browser) |
| `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` | `SECRET_KEY` in `npx supabase status` (server only, never `NEXT_PUBLIC_`) |
| `DATABASE_URL` | `DB_URL` in `npx supabase status` (Prisma at runtime) |
| `DIRECT_URL` | same as `DB_URL` locally (Prisma CLI) |
| `GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY` | shared with the gateway; `test_x_signature_key` locally, matching the brief's test vector |

## Seeded accounts

Every account's password is **`Rent2026!demo`**.

| Organization | Account | Role | Notes |
|---|---|---|---|
| Northwind Properties | manager@northwind.test | manager | |
| Northwind Properties | staff@northwind.test | staff | |
| Northwind Properties | aisyah@northwind.test | tenant | Aisyah Rahman |
| Northwind Properties | ben@northwind.test | tenant | Ben Lim |
| Northwind Properties | probe@northwind.test | tenant | Probe Tenant |
| Beta Realty | manager@beta.test | manager | |
| Beta Realty | chen@beta.test | tenant | Chen Wei |

| Organization | Unit | Tenant | Start | End | Monthly rent | Deposit |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Northwind | A-12-3 | Aisyah Rahman | 2026-01-31 | 2026-07-15 | RM 1,500.00 | RM 3,000.00 |
| Northwind | B-05-1 | Ben Lim | 2026-01-01 | 2026-04-15 | RM 1,000.29 | none |
| Northwind | C-01-7 | Probe Tenant | 2026-02-28 | 2027-02-27 | RM 2,000.00 | RM 4,000.00 |
| Northwind | D-03-2 | (no lease) | | | | |
| Beta | KL-1 | Chen Wei | 2026-03-15 | 2027-03-14 | RM 2,200.00 | RM 4,400.00 |

Aisyah's payments: RM 3,000.00 cash received 2026-01-31 10:00 Malaysia time, recorded by the manager (approved at once); and RM 2,000.00 bank transfer received 2026-03-01 00:30 Malaysia time, recorded by staff with a slip and then approved by the manager. The seed creates leases and payments through the real services (`createLease`, `recordPayment`, `approvePayment`) with the right actor, and uploads the slip as the staff user through the storage policy. Northwind's collections for 2026-01 to 2026-03 are 300000 / 0 / 200000 sen.

## Tests and checks

```bash
npm run lint
npm run typecheck   # next typegen && tsc --noEmit
npm test            # vitest
```

The unit tests cover:

- `src/lib/billing.ts`: the Aisyah worked example, half-up proration (Ben's last period, 50014.5 sen rounds to 50015), anchors on the 31st and on Feb 29, invalid dates and amounts, the overdue boundary at 2026-03-01T16:00:00Z, and the `parseRinggitToSen` vectors. All of it runs under `TZ=UTC`, `Asia/Kuala_Lumpur` and `America/New_York`.
- `src/lib/myt.ts` and the gateway signature, including the brief's test vector.
- Webhook form parsing, the pure allocation planner, error-to-status mapping, and display formatting.

### Concurrency check

[`scripts/concurrency-check.ts`](scripts/concurrency-check.ts) fires truly parallel HTTP requests at a running app, then checks the database. It changes data, so run it on a fresh seed:

```bash
npx supabase db reset && npm run seed
npm run build && npm start         # or npm run dev; keep it running
npm run check:concurrency          # in a second shell; BASE_URL defaults to http://localhost:3000
```

Each race runs for several rounds:

| Race | Expected result |
|---|---|
| Two staff payments on Ben's lease that together exceed the cap | one 201, one 422 |
| Two approves of the same payment | one 200, one 409, allocated once |
| Two overlapping leases on D-03-2 | one 201, one 409, one lease stored |
| Two identical `paid=true` webhook deliveries | 200 and 200, one payment |

The script exits non-zero if any check fails.

## Paying online with the gateway simulator

1. Sign in as a tenant, for example `ben@northwind.test`, and press **Pay now** on the portal. The page shows the new bill id and amount. To create a bill over the API instead, use `POST /api/leases/:leaseId/gateway-bills` with the tenant's Bearer token.
2. Play the gateway:

   ```bash
   GATEWAY_X_SIGNATURE_KEY=test_x_signature_key node gateway-sim.mjs <bill_id> <amount_sen> true
   ```

   Pass `false` instead of `true` for a failed payment. Set `WEBHOOK_URL` to call something other than `http://localhost:3000/api/webhooks/gateway`.
3. Open `/payments/return?bill_id=<bill_id>&paid=true`. The page only reads the bill's status from the database. It ignores `paid` and changes nothing: only the signed webhook settles a bill.

The webhook's responses follow the brief's table:

| Callback | Response |
|---|---|
| Missing or wrong signature | 401 |
| Unknown bill | 404 |
| `paid=true` with the wrong amount | 422 |
| Anything else, including repeat and late deliveries | 200 |

A bill creates at most one payment, ever, and `received_at` is the gateway's `paid_at`.

## What works

- **Billing rules** (`src/lib/billing.ts`): pure and independent of the machine's timezone. The app uses them for lease creation, statuses and payment amounts.
- **HTTP API**: every endpoint in the brief's section 7. They accept a Bearer token or the session cookie, and return 401, 403 and 404 per section 6.
- **Lease creation**: stores the lease and exactly the invoices `generateSchedule` returns, all or nothing. Overlaps on a unit are refused (409), even for simultaneous requests.
- **Payments**:
  - Record with the cap, which counts pending payments.
  - Approve, which re-checks the remaining balance.
  - Reject and void, each with a reason.
  - Allocation by due date, then deposit before rent, then period index; anything left over is stored as `unapplied_sen`.
  - An `audit_log` row for every lease creation, approval, rejection and void.
- **Slips**: private `payment-slips` bucket, stored under `<org_id>/…`. A slip must be a JPEG, PNG or PDF of at most 5 MB. An unused slip is deleted when recording fails, and staff view slips through short-lived signed URLs.
- **Gateway**: unguessable bill ids (128 random bits), a signed webhook with a timing-safe compare, and idempotent, concurrency-safe settlement.
- **Collections report**: totals by Malaysia calendar month, including months with nothing collected.
- **Data API and Storage**:
  - RLS and grants follow the brief's matrix.
  - Anonymous users get nothing.
  - A tenant can update only their own phone number.
  - `audit_log` is append-only for every role, including the table owner.
  - Public signups are disabled.
- **UI**:
  - Staff and managers: dashboard (overdue count, last 6 months of collections), leases list, lease page, and record, approve, reject and void with confirmation and a reason.
  - Tenants: a portal that reads through supabase-js under RLS, amount due now, Pay now, phone editing, and the read-only return page.
  - Every date and time is shown in Malaysia time, whatever the viewer's timezone.

## Known issues

- **Orphaned slips.** If the browser uploads a slip and then loses its connection before it calls the API, the slip stays in the bucket. The server only removes slips when the API call itself fails.
- **Several pending bills per lease.** A tenant can create more than one pending gateway bill for the same lease. If both are paid, the second becomes `unapplied_sen` on its payment.
- **Unapplied credit is never re-applied.** After a void reopens invoices, an online payment's `unapplied_sen` stays where it is, because other payments' allocations do not change. A manager has to sort it out.
- **No FK from `memberships.user_id` / `tenants.user_id` to `auth.users`.** `prisma db pull` rejects cross-schema foreign keys.
- **audit_log isn't tamper-proof against the owner.** Its append-only rule is a trigger, so the database owner could still disable or drop it.
- **Some summaries are computed in application code.** The overdue counts and the leases list do this, which is fine at seed scale but would need SQL aggregation for thousands of invoices.
- **Slip links expire.** They are created when the lease page renders and last 5 minutes; reload the page to get fresh ones.
- **Install scripts are blocked by default.** npm 11 does this for dependencies (esbuild, prisma). The app, tests and seed work without them, but `npm install` prints a warning.

## What I would do next

- A create-lease form with a live schedule preview. Leases are API-only today.
- Server-side search and pagination for the leases list, kept in the URL.
- Realtime updates on the tenant portal when the webhook settles a bill.
- Reuse a lease's open pending bill instead of creating another, and expire stale bills.
- A manager action to apply `unapplied_sen` credit to reopened invoices, recorded in the audit log.
- Integration tests for the API, RLS and Storage in CI, against a disposable Supabase stack.

## Design notes

1. Money is integer sen everywhere: `bigint` columns, `BigInt` in Prisma, `number` only at the JSON edge, and rounding only in `billing.ts`.
2. Every money movement (record, approve, void, webhook settle) runs in one transaction that first runs `SELECT … FOR UPDATE` on the lease row.
3. That lock serialises all payments on a lease, so the cap and balance checks read figures nobody can change before commit.
4. Lock order is always lease, then gateway bill, then invoices. `payments.gateway_bill_id` is UNIQUE as a backstop.
5. Lease overlap is a `btree_gist` exclusion constraint, so concurrent creations are refused by the database (23P01, mapped to 409).
6. RLS and grants are the wall for the Data API and Storage. Helper functions live in an unexposed `app` schema, so `/rpc` exposes nothing.
7. Prisma connects as the owner and bypasses RLS. Authorization happens in code: `getCaller` loads the role from `memberships` / `tenants.user_id`, and the services scope every query.
8. One timezone module, `src/lib/myt.ts`, handles every "today" and every date/instant conversion with a fixed +08:00 and never reads the machine's zone.
9. The collections report groups in SQL by Malaysia midnights (`AT TIME ZONE 'Asia/Kuala_Lumpur'`) with `generate_series`, so empty months appear.
10. `supabase/migrations/*.sql` is the single source of truth. `prisma db pull` regenerates `prisma/schema.prisma` from the database, so they cannot drift.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork runs in the background and keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate. Subagents run in the background; you'll be notified when one completes. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).
